Aurora Networks builds end-to-end access network infrastructure for global cable and broadband service providers: HFC and PON access systems, cable headend optics platforms, CMTS and CCAP gear, Distributed Access Architecture (DAA) devices, optical hubs, nodes and passives, RF and RFoG equipment, and video processing, security and delivery systems. Its ServAssure NXT family adds network performance management, alarm handling and service assurance software on top of that hardware estate. The brand originates with Aurora Networks, Inc., founded in Santa Clara, California in 1999 as a pure-play optical transport supplier to cable operators, backed by Battery Ventures among ten investors across roughly $60M raised, and acquired by Pace plc for $323M in 2013 before passing through ARRIS and CommScope. Aurora Networks is a network equipment vendor rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable API specification. Product and integration documentation, including the ServAssure NXT web service and message-bus integration surfaces, sits behind authenticated customer support portals.

providers.name: Nexthop AI
providers.description: Nexthop AI is a networking infrastructure company building next-generation, highly efficient AI and cloud networking for hyperscalers and neo-cloud operators. Founded by former Arista Networks operations leader Anshul Sadana, it designs scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of large GPU clusters by improving power efficiency, cost, reliability, and speed of deployment. The company raised a $500M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Andreessen Horowitz at a $4.2B valuation and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead. It publishes no public web/REST API surface; this profile captures company identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Insurify
providers.description: Insurify is an insurance comparison marketplace licensed in all 50 U.S. states with real-time API integrations into 120+ carriers (500+ across the carrier network), covering auto, home, renters, pet, commercial auto, life, motorcycle, and travel. Consumers get side-by-side quotes in roughly two minutes and can buy online or through licensed agents. Insurify's Evia AI agent (Expert Virtual Insurance Agent) is a voice-and-chat agent that handles end-to-end shopping conversations with bind-ready quotes and renewal-cycle re-shopping. In February 2026 Insurify launched the insurance industry's first ChatGPT app via OpenAI's app library.

providers.name: Prodigal
providers.description: Prodigal is an AI company building purpose-built agents and intelligence for the loan-servicing and debt-collections industry. Its products include proAgent (end-to-end collections automation across voice and digital), PIE (an intelligence layer trained on more than half a billion consumer-finance interactions), proCollect (omnichannel digital orchestration), proScore (propensity-to-pay scoring from 500+ consumer attributes), proPay (an AI-native self-serve payment portal), proNotes (automated call notes), proInsight (QA automation, scorecards, and revenue analytics), and proAssist (real-time agent assistance). Prodigal serves auto finance, collections, healthcare revenue-cycle management, and lending, integrating with dialers and contact-center platforms such as Five9, Genesys, NICE, TCN, and DialConnect. It is backed by Accel and Menlo Ventures. Prodigal exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: rebtel
providers.description: Rebtel is a Swedish international communications company (Rebtel Networks AB, registered 556680-3622, headquartered in Stockholm) serving the world's roughly two billion international migrants with low-cost international calling, mobile top-up / airtime recharge, and calling cards delivered through its iOS and Android apps. It routes calls over optimized local phone lines to keep prices low. Backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. Rebtel exposes no public developer API or SDK program; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, support, and security.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Xsight Labs
providers.description: Xsight Labs is a fabless semiconductor company redefining AI and cloud connectivity with end-to-end, software-defined silicon for hyperscale data centers. Its X-Series programmable Ethernet switch silicon (X1, X2) delivers 3.2-12.8 Tbps with sub-700ns latency and is programmable through XISA, the first fully open, documented switch instruction set architecture, published under MPLv2. Its E-Series is billed as the industry's first fully software-defined 800G DPU family, placing 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores directly in the data path and programmable with standard Linux tooling (XDP, DPDK, SPDK) with no proprietary SDK. Xsight Labs contributes SONiC platform code and a SAI implementation through its public GitHub organization. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors. The company publishes technical documentation, XISA specifications, and programming examples rather than a hosted web API; no public OpenAPI, REST endpoints, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Arrcus
providers.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Petsapp
providers.description: PetsApp is a veterinary client engagement and practice communication platform used by more than 1,000 veterinary practices worldwide, with millions of pets registered and millions of dollars in payments processed. It gives clinics two-way SMS and in-app messaging, appointment booking, video consultations, digital payments, wellness and health-care plan management, automated reminders, and a lightweight CRM for building client relationships. PetsApp does not publish a public developer portal or open API; API access and documentation are offered privately to technology and PIMS integration partners through its partner program, and its public docs subdomain is a Jira Service Management customer help center rather than API reference documentation.

providers.name: Revie
providers.description: Revie is an AI-powered customer review collection and WhatsApp marketing automation platform for e-commerce businesses, with a focus on the Latin American market. It requests and collects product reviews over WhatsApp (in text, photo, video, and voice-note formats) after a purchase, then applies AI sentiment analysis and keyword grouping to surface customer feedback in a dashboard. Revie also powers WhatsApp marketing campaigns, customer segmentation, and discount incentives, and integrates with Shopify, Tienda Nube, and VTEX storefronts. The company exposes no public developer API or SDK; its product is delivered as installable storefront apps.

providers.name: Firsty
providers.description: Firsty is an Amsterdam-based eSIM and mobile connectivity provider founded in 2023 that positions internet access as a basic human right. Its consumer app delivers free, ad-supported global data alongside affordable Classic (pay-per-GB) and Unlimited (daily/monthly) plans, plus international calling, across 170+ countries with automatic connection to the best available network and no physical SIM required. Firsty has surpassed one million users and lists partnerships with brands including Uber, Grab, Mastercard, KBC and Belfius. Backed by Speedinvest, it is a consumer travel-connectivity app with no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Cloudflare.com
providers.description: cloudflare-com is an alias profile for Cloudflare. The canonical company profile lives at the cloudflare repository in the API Evangelist Network; this entry exists so that the ".com" form of the brand resolves into the same canonical record. Cloudflare's developer surface includes a single unified REST API at api.cloudflare.com covering DNS, zones, SSL/TLS, Workers, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, R2, Pages, Stream, Email Routing, Zero Trust, WAF, Magic Transit, Spectrum, Load Balancing, Analytics, and Account Management. Authentication is via API tokens with scoped permissions or legacy global API keys.

providers.name: Eero
providers.description: eero makes home mesh Wi-Fi systems that are simple, powerful, secure, and reliable. eero pioneered home mesh wifi and sells products for homes, businesses, service providers, pro installers, and communities, including the eero Pro 7, eero PoE 7, and eero Signal, plus the eero Plus subscription for enhanced security and multi-network management. Devices are managed through the award-winning eero app and are deployed across 27+ countries. eero LLC is based in San Francisco, CA and is an Amazon company. eero does not publish a public developer API or first-party SDK; the eero app communicates with a private, unpublished backend.

providers.name: DomScan
providers.description: Domain intelligence API for domain availability, DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, valuation, security checks, email posture, social handle checks, and monitoring workflows. Offers REST API, machine-readable contracts, a hosted MCP server, and llms.txt.

providers.name: instabridge
providers.description: Instabridge is a global internet connectivity company operated by Degoo Backup AB in Stockholm, Sweden, and backed by Balderton Capital and Creandum. Its mobile apps give users access to a crowdsourced map of roughly 20 million free WiFi hotspots and to prepaid eSIM mobile-data plans covering 190+ countries with no roaming fees. With more than 200 million app downloads, Instabridge combines community-shared WiFi, pay-as-you-go global data, a data-saving browser, VPN, and cloud storage, and runs a distribution-partner program for prepaid top-up resellers. It is a consumer app company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: VeriSign
providers.description: VeriSign is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The VeriSign API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Cloudgenix
providers.description: CloudGenix was a cloud-native SD-WAN (software-defined wide area network) company founded in 2013 and backed by Mayfield. Its AppFabric platform let enterprises build application-defined, policy-driven WANs managed from a cloud controller, with a full REST API (the CloudGenix Cloud Controller / AppFabric API) and first-party SDKs in Python, C#, Java, and JavaScript plus a CI-capable configuration CLI. Palo Alto Networks acquired CloudGenix in April 2020 for more than $420M and rebranded the product as Prisma SD-WAN, now part of the Prisma SASE portfolio. The public developer tooling remains published under the official CloudGenix GitHub organization.

providers.name: Earn.com
providers.description: Earn.com was a cryptocurrency startup founded in 2013 as 21e6 and later known as 21 Inc and 21.co, backed by a16z and others, which raised over $116 million. It began as a Bitcoin mining venture selling the 21 Bitcoin Computer, then pivoted to a paid-messaging marketplace where senders paid recipients in cryptocurrency to read and reply to email. Coinbase acquired Earn.com in April 2018 for a reported $120 million, and co-founder Balaji Srinivasan became Coinbase's first Chief Technology Officer. The standalone Earn.com product was retired and the brand was folded into Coinbase Earn, the learn-and-earn program. As of July 2026 the earn.com domain issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect for every path to https://www.coinbase.com/earn, and no developer, documentation, or API subdomain resolves. Earn.com therefore has no independent API surface; any remaining API capability lives under Coinbase.

providers.name: Textsidekick
providers.description: Textsidekick (Sidekick) is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) workforce communication and knowledge-management platform built for frontline workers who do not have a desk. Workers text a question or report an issue over plain SMS with no app to install and no login; Sidekick triages the message, answers from company knowledge, converts issues into work orders, routes them to the right person, and captures every fix as searchable organizational knowledge. It also AI-generates safety procedures, handbooks, and FAQs, schedules preventive maintenance, and delivers text-based onboarding and training. Founded to serve the roughly 80% of American workers without a desk, it is live across 20+ plants serving 600+ frontline workers. No public developer API, SDK, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Five9
providers.description: Five9 is a leading cloud contact center (CCaaS) platform providing inbound, outbound, blended, and omnichannel customer engagement with intelligent virtual agents, workforce optimization, agent assist, and analytics. Five9 exposes multiple developer APIs including REST APIs for configuration and reporting, SOAP-based Configuration and Statistics Web Services, the Agent and Supervisor REST APIs (app.five9.com/appsvcs), and Voicestream/event APIs, with authentication via session login and API user credentials.

providers.name: Tinstop Website Intelligence API
providers.description: A keyless, machine-payable Website Intelligence API for domain security and performance audits, built for AI agents. Access is gated per-request via the x402 payment protocol using USDC on Base — no accounts or API keys. Offers 16 pay-per-call endpoints covering DNS/SSL/TLS checks, email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), HTTP security headers, web performance (PageSpeed), domain recon, and AI-generated audit reports.

providers.name: VCNC
providers.description: VCNC is a South Korean mobile technology company behind Between, a private messaging and photo-sharing app for couples, and TADA, a ride-hailing and mobility service operating in Korea. A 500 Global portfolio company, VCNC maintains an open source presence on GitHub, including Haeinsa, a multi-row transaction library for HBase published on Maven Central. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API client SDKs.

providers.name: AirPR
providers.description: AirPR is a public relations analytics and media measurement company whose software helped communications teams quantify the business impact of earned media, tie coverage to web traffic and conversions, and benchmark share of voice against competitors. AirPR is now part of Onclusive, the media intelligence platform that monitors and enriches conversations across 3M+ online sources, 70K+ print outlets, 6K+ broadcast channels, and 25+ social platforms for PR, communications, and marketing professionals. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DubClub
providers.description: DubClub is an all-in-one platform to create and join sports betting communities. It is a marketplace connecting sports betting content creators known as cappers or handicappers with subscribers who want timely, reliable betting picks and analysis. Creators monetize their expertise by selling picks and predictions through paid subscriptions, while subscribers receive content directly via notifications and messaging rather than scattered across social media and Discord. DubClub has facilitated tens of millions in payments for creators and delivered hundreds of millions of messages containing informational sports betting content. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital; DubClub publishes a consumer web product and does not expose a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: EdSights
providers.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

providers.name: Moxtra
providers.description: Moxtra (now operating as Moxo) is a contextual collaboration and customer engagement platform that lets businesses embed chat, video meetings, voice calls, file sharing, e-signature, digital workflows, and binder-based collaboration into their own mobile and web applications via SDKs and REST APIs. The Moxtra Developer Portal exposes 200+ REST API endpoints for managing users, binders (workspaces), messages, files, meetings, todos, and notifications. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 access tokens issued against the Moxtra (or self-branded GroupHour) authorization server.

providers.name: Pindrop
providers.description: Pindrop is a voice and audio security company providing a continuous identity verification and deepfake-detection platform for enterprises. Its technology authenticates callers and video-meeting participants, detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and fraudulent activity, and protects contact centers, virtual meetings, and connected devices. Pindrop's products span call-center fraud detection, passive voice authentication, and liveness/deepfake defense, and are delivered largely through partner platforms (Amazon Connect, Zoom, Webex, and others) rather than a public self-service developer API. The company is backed by Felicis, GV, and IVP and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Sidechat
providers.description: Sidechat is an anonymous, campus-based social networking app for college students, built by Flower Ave Inc in New York City and backed by Canaan Partners. Students verify with a school email to join their college's private, location- and campus-scoped community where they post text, images, and polls, vote, and chat anonymously in a Reddit-like feed. Sidechat launched in early 2022, acquired Yik Yak in 2023, and operates primarily as an iOS consumer app. It publishes no official public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures the company's public web presence and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Storyboard
providers.description: Storyboard is a fleet-operations AI platform that gives trucking and logistics companies voice-first, hands-free AI workers for their drivers. The system automates dispatch updates, driver coaching, safety alerts, and compliance monitoring (including hours-of-service and idling) so back-office teams field fewer phone calls and drivers stay hands-free on the road. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, Storyboard began as an enterprise podcast and internal-audio communication platform (a $4.5M seed round led by CRV in 2020) before pivoting to AI-powered fleet operations. It is distributed through in-cab telematics marketplaces such as Platform Science and ISAAC Instruments. Storyboard exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is via its web and mobile apps at app.storyboard.com. This profile was surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Tagged
providers.description: Tagged is a social discovery and dating platform founded in 2004 and based in San Francisco, where members browse profiles of people nearby or worldwide, chat, play social games, exchange tags and virtual gifts, and make new connections. Originally a standalone social network backed by early investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), Tagged was acquired by MeetMe in 2017 for roughly 60 million dollars and today operates as a consumer brand within The Meet Group (part of the ParshipMeet Group) alongside apps such as MeetMe, Skout, and LOVOO. The current tagged.com is a consumer-facing web and mobile social-dating experience with no public developer program or API; a legacy REST-style API (tagged.com/api.php) that once powered third-party integrations has been retired. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Fibraweb, S.p.a.
providers.description: Fibraweb S.p.A. is an Italian telecommunications infrastructure operator, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Perugia (Umbria), that designs, builds and operates its own fiber-optic access network for businesses, wholesale operators and public administrations. The company delivers FTTH/FTTB ultra-broadband internet access, dedicated internet access circuits, and local and long-distance voice/telephony services across the Umbria, Marche, Toscana and Lazio regions, with a proprietary network of roughly 1,500 km of fiber reaching 150 industrial zones and the ability to connect over 30,000 companies. Fibraweb is a Battery Ventures portfolio company (investors also include Equiter and GTD Grupo Teleductos) and holds ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 certifications. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Dycom Industries
providers.description: Dycom Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Dycom Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Mastra
providers.description: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI-powered applications and agents, built by the team behind Gatsby (Sam Bhagwat, Abhi Aiyer, Shane Thomas). The framework provides production-grade primitives for agents, workflows, RAG, tools, memory, evals, voice, and observability, and integrates with 40+ model providers through the Vercel AI SDK. The framework is Apache 2.0 licensed open source, with a hosted commercial offering (Mastra Cloud) for deployment, tracing, and team collaboration, and an enterprise self-hosted edition for regulated environments.

providers.name: Mobileum
providers.description: Mobileum is a telecom analytics and intelligence software vendor whose Active Intelligence Platform delivers AI-powered decisioning, risk management, and network insight for mobile network operators. Its product families span roaming management (traffic steering, GlobalRoamer, campaign management), risk management (revenue assurance and fraud detection via RAID), network security (cross-protocol signaling firewalls and SMS/voice protection), testing and service assurance (5G, eSIM, IoT, VoLTE testing, dsTest), customer experience, and data insights and monetization. Mobileum sells primarily to carriers as deployed/managed enterprise software and does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface.

providers.name: Suno
providers.description: Suno is a Cambridge, Massachusetts-based generative AI music company building a consumer platform that lets anyone create original songs from natural language prompts. The product spans text-to-song generation, vocal and instrumental tracks, style and genre control, stem splitting, audio upload and remixing, lyric writing, and Suno Studio for advanced multi-track editing and custom model tuning. The company runs proprietary foundation models for music generation, the latest being v5.5, and ships consumer subscription plans (Free, Pro, Premier) with commercial usage rights on paid tiers. Founded in 2021 by Mikey Shulman, Georg Kucsko, Martin Camacho, and Keenan Freyberg, Suno closed a $250M Series C in November 2025 at a $2.45B valuation led by Menlo Ventures with participation from NVentures, Hallwood Media, Lightspeed, and Matrix. The company has announced a partnership with Warner Music Group. Suno does not publish an official developer API or SDK; the consumer surface is web and mobile applications authenticated via account login, and any third-party "Suno API" offerings are unofficial reverse-engineered wrappers. The suno-ai GitHub organization hosts the open-source Bark text-to-audio model and supporting tooling rather than a Suno product SDK.

providers.name: Cignara
providers.description: Cignara is an enterprise AI platform that replaces traditional customer support (FAQ bots and IVR menus) with governed voice and chat AI agents that serve, sell, and grow. Its agents handle inbound and outbound phone and chat conversations end to end across 32+ languages, pulling customer context, applying business policy, executing transactions (checkout, scheduling, refunds, retention), and offering a real-time human copilot for support teams. The platform emphasizes in-region data sovereignty and hallucination-free, policy-bound actions grounded in each enterprise's own knowledge base. Founded 2026 (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) in San Francisco; legal entity ShopAdvisor Inc.

providers.name: Vanu
providers.description: Vanu, Inc. builds wireless network solutions that extend cellular coverage to areas that cannot be profitably served with conventional technology - rural regions, buildings, tunnels, and maritime environments. Founded in 1998 out of MIT software-radio research and headquartered in Lexington, MA (with offices in Gurgaon, Bangalore, and Kigali), Vanu ships the Anywave dual-mode GSM/LTE base station (the first FCC-certified software-defined radio), Community Connect village systems, portable LTE networks, VanuMaps coverage mapping, and coverage-as-a-service for mobile carriers, with deployments across rural India, Rwanda, and post-hurricane Puerto Rico and partnerships with Amazon Leo / Project Kuiper. Vanu publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Highway 9 Networks
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks delivers AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service, providing secure private mobile networks and deterministic 5G connectivity for enterprise AI workloads. Its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), distributed edge running a 5G core and AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device and robot fleets (Mobile Zones) to give autonomous robots, cameras, and edge devices ultra-reliable, ultra-low-latency connectivity across manufacturing, warehousing, higher education, and energy environments. Highway 9 exposes Mobile Center streaming APIs for orchestration, telemetry, device management, alerting, and analytics, though the full specification is available only through its partner portal for signed partners. The company is backed by Mayfield and was added to the API Evangelist network as an enriched provider profile.

providers.name: Mia
providers.description: Mia (Mia Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered phone agent platform built specifically for automotive dealerships. Its conversational voice AI answers calls 24/7 across sales, service, reception, and outbound operations, handling appointment scheduling, service booking, lead capture, and recall/follow-up outreach over phone, SMS, and voice with automatic multi-language detection. Mia integrates with major dealership platforms and DMS/CRM systems including Tekion, CDK, Reynolds & Reynolds, and Dealertrack, and reports use across 350+ dealerships. The company raised a $20M Series A (roughly $29M total) backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Permanent Capital Ventures. This profile currently covers the company identity; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Nile
providers.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

providers.name: Nova Labs
providers.description: Nova Labs, Inc. is the company behind the Helium Network, a decentralized wireless network that replaces traditional carrier infrastructure with community-hosted Hotspots and is coordinated on the Solana blockchain and incentivized with the HNT token. Helium operates two networks: a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular/Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). Nova Labs open-sources the network's protocol surface as gRPC/Protobuf service definitions (the helium/proto config, router, and proof-of-coverage services) and publishes a set of first-party client libraries, a command-line tool, and Rust crates for cryptography and protobuf types. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from Nova Labs' public developer surface; much of the legacy Helium IoT REST API tooling is archived following the network's migration to Solana.

providers.name: August AI
providers.description: August AI is a consumer health-AI companion that helps people understand their symptoms, lab reports, prescriptions, and medications, and connects them to licensed physicians through asynchronous, chat-based telehealth visits. Founded in 2022 by Anuruddh Mishra after a four-month misdiagnosis, August operates as a 24/7 health assistant available on iOS, Android, and WhatsApp, storing lab reports and conversation history in long-term memory to deliver personalized guidance. The service pairs a free AI symptom-assessment experience with paid online doctor consultations from board-certified MDs licensed across all 50 US states. August reports serving millions of users across 160+ countries in 30+ languages, and publishes medical benchmarks including 100% accuracy on the USMLE, 97.4% on MedQA, 99.4% on lab-report document processing, and 100% precision/recall on emergency escalation. It is backed by Accel and Claypond Capital. August is a consumer application and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Bloxtel, Inc.
providers.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.

providers.name: CarNow
providers.description: CarNow is an AI-enabled conversion platform built specifically for automotive dealerships, helping them turn more website visitors into leads, more leads into sales, and more buyers into lifelong service customers. Its product suite spans website solutions (AI-powered chat, digital retail, and shop-by-payment experiences), sales follow-up automation (Cruise Control, which prioritizes high-intent shoppers and automates nurture workflows), and service retention (Lane Assist, which drives post-sale engagement and service scheduling). CarNow works with more than 4,000 dealer partners and integrates with major OEM programs including Acura, Audi, BMW, Ford, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Land Rover, and Lexus. The company is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and is backed by Battery Ventures. CarNow does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its api.carnow.com endpoint is a partner/internal AWS API Gateway that requires authentication.

providers.name: Nexthop AI
providers.description: Nexthop AI (Nexthop Systems Inc.) builds efficient AI networking infrastructure for the world's largest cloud operators. Founded by Anshul Sadana, the company designs scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered for hyperscalers and neoclouds, focused on power efficiency, cost, reliability, and speed of deployment to bring down the cost per token of AI workloads. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the company raised an oversubscribed $500M Series B at a $4.2B valuation. This is a hardware and systems networking company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API reference — its login surface is a customer support and software-release portal, not a public programmable API.

providers.name: Nexthop Systems
providers.description: Nexthop AI (Nexthop Systems) builds power-efficient AI networking infrastructure for hyperscalers and NeoClouds — scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of training and serving large AI models. Founded and led by CEO Anshul Sadana, the company is backed by Battery Ventures and raised an oversubscribed $500M Series B in 2025 at a $4.2 billion valuation. Nexthop runs a public marketing, blog and news site plus a login-gated customer Support Hub and Learning Hub; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: UpSmith
providers.description: UpSmith is a Dallas, Texas-based company backed by a16z that builds AI agents for home services and skilled trades businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical). Its platform texts customers to confirm appointments, follows up on cold estimates, responds to inbound leads around the clock, and reactivates dormant customers, syncing customer records, job details, and booking data with ServiceTitan through ServiceTitan's official APIs. UpSmith consumes partner APIs (a native ServiceTitan marketplace integration) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Umony
providers.description: Umony is a London-based communications compliance platform, founded in 2017 and backed by Seedcamp, that captures, records, and archives employee voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and Microsoft Teams conversations at the telecom-network level for banks and other regulated financial institutions. Its platform spans the Umony App (BYOD softphone), Umony Mobile (eSIM carrier-level capture), and Umony Archive with AI risk scoring, and the company holds BSI-certified ISO 27001:2022, ISO 42001:2023, and ISO 22301:2019 certifications. Umony publishes no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: ATOM
providers.description: Atom (atomchat.io) is a Panama-based conversational-commerce platform whose multimodal AI Agents combine text, voice, image, and CRM data to run human-like WhatsApp conversations that qualify leads and close sales for businesses across Latin America. Founded in 2019 by Erick Holmann and Rene Mouynes and backed by Techstars and Mucker Capital, Atom connects WhatsApp click-to-chat ads to an AI agent that engages and qualifies prospects, then hands sales-ready leads to human reps. It exposes a Customers API and a WhatsApp template-message API, both authenticated with an account API key configured from the Atom admin panel.

providers.name: Nurix AI
providers.description: Nurix AI is an enterprise conversational-AI company that builds human-like voice and chat AI agents for sales, customer support, and internal operations. Founded by Mukesh Bansal and backed by Accel and General Catalyst, Nurix delivers custom AI agents across voice, chat, email, SMS, and social channels through its NuPlay conversational-AI platform, NuStack workflow engine, and NuPulse conversation-analytics product. It serves 30+ enterprises across retail, insurance, financial services, healthcare, and education, and offers enterprise-grade security controls (PII redaction, RBAC, SSO, audit trails, and regional data residency) with a HIPAA (BAA), DPA, and GDPR compliance posture. Nurix acquired the conversational-support platform Verloop.io. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: AST SpaceMobile
providers.description: AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ, ASTS) is a United States satellite operator building the SpaceMobile Network, a space-based cellular broadband constellation of BlueBird satellites carrying the largest commercial phased-array antennas in low Earth orbit, designed to deliver 4G and 5G directly to standard, unmodified smartphones. It sits upstream of the retail telecom market as a wholesale coverage layer, not a consumer brand, not a CPaaS: signals from a handset are relayed by satellite to a small number of in-country ground gateways, which compensate for Doppler and delay and then hand the traffic into a mobile network operator's core, where the operator completes the call and bills the subscriber. Distribution runs entirely through partner carriers, with agreements covering nearly 60 mobile network operators serving over 3 billion subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten, Bell, TELUS and stc, plus strategic investment from Google and American Tower. Its API posture is that of a satellite infrastructure company rather than a network-API publisher, honestly assessed as none: as of July 2026 AST SpaceMobile publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no public network-API surface. Probes of developer, developers, docs, api and opengateway subdomains and the corresponding site paths all fail to resolve or return 404, and no CAMARA, GSMA Open Gateway, TM Forum or 3GPP NEF exposure claim appears anywhere on ast-science.com or in its press releases. Any programmable access to SpaceMobile capacity reaches developers only indirectly, through the partner carrier that owns the subscriber relationship and the network APIs.

providers.name: Execthread
providers.description: ExecThread is a selective, invitation-based network where successful executives discreetly share confidential, recruiter-led job opportunities with one another that are not posted on public job boards. The membership platform matches vetted senior professionals with unadvertised executive-level roles, offers executive branding services and resume review, and runs a points-based referral economy for members who contribute opportunities. Founded as a private career marketplace, it has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 and by the Financial Times. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it exposes no public API or developer surface as of this profile.

providers.name: OpenDNS
providers.description: OpenDNS is a cloud-delivered recursive DNS and internet security service founded in 2005 and acquired by Cisco in 2015, where its enterprise capabilities now form the foundation of the Cisco Umbrella platform. OpenDNS continues to offer free consumer products - OpenDNS Home and OpenDNS Family Shield - providing recursive DNS resolution, phishing and malware blocking, and content filtering with parental controls across every device on a home network, all managed through the OpenDNS dashboard. Enterprise DNS-layer security, secure web gateway, and the Investigate threat-intelligence API have migrated to Cisco Umbrella (umbrella.cisco.com). Added to the API Evangelist network as a Greylock portfolio company in the cybersecurity sector.

providers.name: Rylo
providers.description: Rylo (Nagish Inc. d/b/a Rylo) is a New York-based accessibility technology company building free communication tools for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability. Its consumer mobile app provides FCC-certified real-time phone-call captioning, in-person Live Transcribe, and Sign features, with automatic language detection across 50+ languages. Rylo raised $85M and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. The company operates a consumer application only and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Remind
providers.description: Remind is a K-12 school-home communication platform that lets teachers, schools, and districts message students and families by text, app, email, and voice without exchanging personal phone numbers. The product line includes Remind Chat, a free two-way messaging service used by individual teachers and classrooms, and Remind Hub, a paid district-wide communications platform with administrative controls, SIS integration, delivery analytics, and translation into 90+ languages. Remind reports use in roughly 80% of US public schools and by a majority of US teachers. In November 2023, Santa Barbara-based ParentSquare acquired Remind, and the combined company now operates under the ParentSquare name with Remind Hub continuing for existing district customers and Remind Chat continuing for classroom-level use; Remind Tutoring was discontinued as part of the combination. Remind's only externally documented developer surface is the Share on Remind SDK (the "Remind Share SDK"), a partner program that lets approved third-party content providers embed the Remind composer into their own product, authenticate Remind users via OAuth 2.0, serve shareable content and previews via partner-hosted webhooks, and ship messages back through Remind. The Share SDK is accessed by application through partners@remind.com and the developer console at remind.com/integrations; there is no public self-serve REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no general-purpose messaging API for sending Remind messages from third-party systems.

providers.name: Skout
providers.description: Skout is a location-based social discovery and dating mobile app that lets people meet, chat, and make connections with others nearby or worldwide. Operated by the ParshipMeet Group, Skout is distributed as consumer iOS and Android applications and an in-browser experience, and was an early a16z portfolio company. It is a consumer product with no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or API surface; this profile captures its public identity and published legal/support pages. Added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Clubhouse
providers.description: Clubhouse (Alpha Exploration Co.) is a social audio application founded in 2020 by Paul Davison and Rohan Seth, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Kindred Ventures. It popularized live "drop-in" audio chat rooms where people gather to talk, listen, and learn in real time across clubs, channels, and scheduled events. Clubhouse ships consumer iOS and Android apps and operates its service on the clubhouse.com / clubhouseapi.com domains. The company does not publish an official, documented public developer API or SDK; the only machine-readable interfaces are third-party, reverse-engineered clients maintained by the community and not endorsed by Alpha Exploration Co. This API Evangelist profile captures the provider's real public surface — website, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe — with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: Prosimo
providers.description: Prosimo is a multi-cloud networking platform that gives enterprises a full-stack cloud transit, security, performance, observability, and cost-management layer across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. Its Application eXperience Infrastructure (AXI) abstracts cloud-provider networking constructs and ties network transit, micro-segmentation, zero-trust policy, WAF, and observability into an autonomous, ML-driven control plane. Prosimo exposes that control plane programmatically through a first-party Terraform provider (prosimo-io/prosimo) for full lifecycle management of cloud gateways, network and application onboarding, policies, namespaces, and security profiles; a companion Pulumi bridge repository and reusable Terraform modules are published on GitHub. Prosimo was venture-backed by General Catalyst, WRVI Capital, and BlackRock; industry sources report it was subsequently acquired by Palo Alto Networks.

providers.name: Achronix Semiconductor
providers.description: Achronix Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-performance FPGA (field-programmable gate array) products and embedded FPGA (eFPGA) intellectual property. Its portfolio includes the Speedster7t family of standalone FPGAs, Speedcore eFPGA IP for system-on-chip integration, VectorPath PCIe accelerator cards, and the ACE design tools suite for synthesis, verification, and optimization. Achronix technology targets AI/ML inference, 5G/6G networking, data-center compute acceleration, automotive, SmartNICs, and test-and-measurement workloads. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Battery Ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API or developer API portal; its developer surface is a hardware support portal, product documentation, datasheets, and design tools.

providers.name: Luzia
providers.description: Luzia is a consumer-facing artificial intelligence assistant serving 85M+ users across web, iOS, Android, desktop, and WhatsApp, with a strong presence in Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking markets where it ranks as the #1 app in several countries. The free assistant offers AI chat, image generation, PDF understanding, web search, and an agentic "LuziClaw" task mode, with a Luzia+ premium subscription adding advanced reasoning, custom AI characters, and higher generation limits. Luzia is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, Luzia publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: MaxLinear
providers.description: MaxLinear, Inc. (NASDAQ: MXL) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Carlsbad, California that designs radio-frequency (RF), high-performance analog, and mixed-signal communications systems-on-chip (SoCs) for critical network infrastructure, the connected home, and industrial and multi-market applications. Its products integrate RF, analog, mixed-signal, digital signal processing, security engines, data compression, networking, and power management into single chips that power cable and fiber broadband modems, Wi-Fi 6/7 and wireline home routers, optical transceivers, 4G/5G base-station and backhaul infrastructure, and high-speed data-center interconnects. MaxLinear exposes developer surface primarily as hardware/firmware SDKs and C APIs (for example the Panther Storage Acceleration SDK and the MxL890x Raw Acceleration API) delivered with its silicon, along with design tools, simulation models, and a technical documentation library — it does not publish a public web/REST API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: swivl
providers.description: swivl is an AI automation platform built specifically for the self-storage industry. It combines a unified CRM and contact center that consolidates calls, texts, emails, and chats with AI agents for sales, billing, support, and review management, plus a tenant mobile app (Spot) for access codes, payments, and referrals. Its self-storage natural-language model is trained on hundreds of thousands of customer conversations and serves 3,500+ locations. Founded in New York City and backed by Techstars, swivl advertises open APIs and integrations with major self-storage management systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: getriff
providers.description: Riff (getriff.co) is a voice and video workspace for remote and hybrid teams, backed by Balderton Capital. Its Mac and Windows desktop apps aim to reduce Slack overload and Zoom fatigue with a minimal video header, one-click availability-based chat, multi-screen sharing with drawing tools, advanced echo cancellation, and focus-time scheduling that updates status automatically, plus Google Calendar and Slack integrations. Riff ships as a consumer/team desktop product and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, legal, and domain-security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital.

providers.name: Hi Marley
providers.description: Hi Marley is an intelligent conversational platform built for the property and casualty (P&C) insurance industry, delivering carrier-to-policyholder communication over SMS. The platform connects carriers, policyholders, and service providers through a single messaging fabric to streamline claims — including Conversational FNOL (First Notice of Loss) intake, Total Loss Assist for auto claims, and Workflow Assist for property claims — layered with AI coaching, sentiment analysis, and data insights. Trusted by 130+ carriers, including four of the top ten U.S. insurers across auto, property, and workers compensation lines. Hi Marley is backed by Emergence Capital and True Ventures. No public developer platform, API documentation, or self-service onboarding was found; the product is delivered as a closed SaaS to insurance carriers.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Zapia
providers.description: Zapia is a personal AI assistant built for Latin America by BrainLogic AI (a Uruguay/Silicon Valley startup), delivered inside WhatsApp and as native Android and iOS apps plus a Flutter web app at app.zapia.com. It engages consumers in hyper-localized, natural-language conversations to compare prices, reply to and transcribe WhatsApp messages and voice notes, organize calendars (with Google Calendar sync), make reservations, and discover nearby businesses using BrainLogic's database of millions of Latin American business WhatsApp numbers. Zapia runs on Claude via Google Cloud Vertex AI and has surpassed 5.5 million users across the region, backed by seed funding led by Prosus Ventures. It is a consumer (B2C) product: as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal — this profile captures its public identity and consumer-facing surfaces.

providers.name: Skyworks Solutions
providers.description: Skyworks Solutions, Inc. is an American semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California that designs, develops, and markets proprietary semiconductor products for wireless communications, automotive, broadband, connected home, industrial, defense, and consumer electronics applications. Skyworks is a leading provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, with dominant market share in 5G RF front-end modules (35% market share). Products span amplifiers, filters, front-end modules, isolators, switches, and power management ICs serving mobile, automotive, IoT, and infrastructure markets. The company does not publish a public developer API but provides datasheets, evaluation tools, and design resources for hardware engineers.

providers.name: Affirmed Networks
providers.description: Affirmed Networks is a cloud-native mobile core networking company, acquired by Microsoft in 2020 and now operating as part of the Azure for Operators initiative. It builds virtualized, fully software-based mobile network functions for telecommunications operators, including a Virtual Evolved Packet Core (vEPC), the Affirmed UnityCloud 5G Core, private network services, network slicing, and analytics. Its packet-core technology underpins Microsoft's Azure Operator Nexus and Azure Operator 5G Core platforms. Affirmed serves carriers and service providers modernizing their networks and does not expose a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: David AI
providers.description: David AI is an audio data research company building high-quality speech and conversational datasets to bring AI into the real world through voice. Using a rigorous six-step research process (hypothesize, design, experiment, evaluate, productionize, release), the team produces datasets such as Converse (channel-separated two-speaker English conversations), Atlas (multilingual data spanning 15+ languages with dialect and accent metadata), Chorus (multi-speaker conversations for speaker separation and diarization), and Dialog (expert domain conversations). Its data is licensed to Fortune 100 companies and research labs working on speech recognition, translation, synthesis, and conversational AI. Access is arranged through samples, consultation, and a data license agreement rather than a self-serve API. David AI is backed by Amplify Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Nagish
providers.description: Nagish (now operating as Rylo, following an $85M raise and rebrand) is a free phone-call captioning and live-transcription service for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability. Originally launched as the Nagish app (talknagish.com), the FCC-certified service delivers real-time captions on incoming and outgoing calls, in-person Live Transcribe, voicemail captioning, 50+ language support, and AI-powered quick replies, with transcripts kept private on-device. It is a consumer mobile/telecom product and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Canaan Partners and Techstars; profiled in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Owl Labs
providers.description: Owl Labs is a Boston-based video conferencing hardware and software company building smart devices for hybrid meetings. Its flagship Meeting Owl line is a 360-degree AI-powered camera, microphone, and speaker that automatically focuses on whoever is speaking, alongside accessories such as the Owl Bar, Whiteboard Owl, and Expansion Mic. The Nest is its cloud fleet-management platform for provisioning, updating, and monitoring deployed devices across an organization. Owl Labs sells to enterprises, schools, and distributed teams, and publishes an annual State of Hybrid Work report. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and Playground Global. Owl Labs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: RetainIQ
providers.description: RetainIQ is a full-service retention-marketing agency for direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, delivering lifecycle email and SMS programs. Its work spans automated flows (welcome, cart abandonment, post-purchase, win-back, replenishment), weekly strategic campaign sends with design and copywriting, and deliverability/segmentation/list-hygiene infrastructure. A proprietary 1:1 personalization engine generates variant product blocks at scale. A Klaviyo Gold Master Partner and Omnisend partner, RetainIQ integrates with Shopify, Klaviyo, and Omnisend; plans start at $990/mo on month-to-month terms. It operates as a marketing-services agency and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: SpectrumOutage API
providers.description: Community-powered REST API for live Spectrum internet, TV, and phone outage data across the US. Independent tracker, not affiliated with Charter Communications or Spectrum. Provides aggregate stats, outage reports, city/state/ZIP status, and map pin data.

providers.name: Volley
providers.description: Volley is a San Francisco voice-AI entertainment company, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that builds voice-controlled and connected-TV games. Its catalog includes hits such as Song Quiz, Yes Sire, and officially licensed titles like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and Family Feud, playable on Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Roku, Fire TV, LG, and Samsung TVs. The company is rebranding its consumer surface as "Weekend." Volley operates as a consumer entertainment product studio and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Discz
providers.description: Discz is a consumer mobile application that blends music discovery with social chat, styled as a modern, MySpace-inspired music community. Users discover songs, build music profiles, and chat with others around shared taste in music. The iOS app is developed by Discz, a Y Combinator-backed startup and a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. Discz publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is the consumer iOS app distributed through the Apple App Store.

providers.name: enrich
providers.description: Enrich is a private, invite-only membership network for senior technology leaders — VPs, Directors, and CXOs from companies including Google, Slack, Anthropic, and OpenAI. It runs peer-led conversations with executive coaching, curated small-group and monthly in-person dinners, expert-led operator discussions, topic-based peer groups (organizational design, career transitions), and a private Slack community for real-time peer advice. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Cowboy Ventures, and added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. Enrich publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — it is a community/membership product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Zoho Meeting
providers.description: Zoho Meeting is an online meeting, video conferencing, and webinar platform from Zoho that lets teams host secure meetings, presentations, and recorded webinars from any device. The Zoho Meeting REST API enables programmatic scheduling, management, and reporting of meetings and webinars, including registrant handling and session lifecycle. Authentication uses Zoho's OAuth 2.0 (Zoho-oauthtoken) with domain-specific API endpoints.

providers.name: Kik
providers.description: Kik is a freeware instant-messaging mobile app for iOS and Android, known for letting users register with only a username rather than a phone number. Founded in 2009 by University of Waterloo students and released in 2010, Kik grew to hundreds of millions of registered users and was especially popular with teens. It has been owned by MediaLab AI since 2019. Kik formerly operated a developer surface — the Kik Bot Platform at dev.kik.com — and the Kin cryptocurrency, but that developer/bot API platform is no longer online and Kik currently publishes no public API.

providers.name: Tomo
providers.description: Tomo is a consumer "personal AI" application that lives in your text messages: users tell Tomo about their life, goals, problems, and aspirations over SMS, and the AI assistant learns those goals and guides them toward achieving them through ongoing text-based conversation. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Ribbit Capital, Tomo operates in the AI-apps sector as a mobile-first consumer product rather than a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site (tomo.ai) with About, Careers, Privacy, Terms, and Login pages but no public developer program: no API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, llms.txt, or .well-known discovery endpoints were found. This profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: All City Communications
providers.description: All City Communications is a Wisconsin-based telephone answering and call center service provider offering 24/7 live answering for businesses across many industries. Founded in 1979 (originally as a paging service), the company operates from Green Bay and Milwaukee and delivers custom call scripting, message delivery by text, email or live call patching, call recording with secure storage, a customer web portal for real-time call data, and detailed call reporting. It serves property management, home restoration, electrical / plumbing / HVAC trades, municipalities, home health and hospice, healthcare, legal, landscaping, and travel and hospitality clients. All City Communications is a service business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: West Technology Group
providers.description: West Technology Group is a cloud-based global technology company providing customer experience and communications solutions through its WestCX platform. The company operates through two main brands: Mosaicx, which delivers AI-native conversational automation for enterprise customer engagement, and TeleVox, which provides digital patient engagement solutions for healthcare organizations including providers, payers, and life sciences companies.

providers.name: Kiki
providers.description: Kiki (Kikihub) is a location-based social networking and chat mobile app that connects people nearby for local friendships, dating, networking, and community conversations. Users join local chat rooms to discover people around them and start real conversations, meeting new friends and matches in their area. The app is available for iOS and Android. Kiki publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed (500 Global, a16z) consumer social lead awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: MeetMe
providers.description: MeetMe is a consumer social-discovery and chat platform that helps people find and connect with new people nearby who share their interests, through profiles, feeds, live streaming, and real-time messaging on web and mobile. Operated by The Meet Group as part of the ParshipMeet Group, MeetMe grew out of the myYearbook social network and today runs as a location-aware social networking and dating-adjacent app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MeetMe publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Tejas Networks India
providers.description: Tejas Networks is a Bengaluru, India-based optical and data networking products company that designs, develops and manufactures telecom networking equipment for communications service providers, internet and cable operators, utilities, defence and government agencies worldwide. Its portfolio spans optical transport (DWDM/OTN), packet transport, broadband access (GPON/fiber) and wireless (4G/5G radio access) systems deployed across more than 75 countries. The company is publicly listed in India (NSE/BSE TEJASNET) and is majority owned by the Tata Group; Battery Ventures was an early institutional investor. Tejas Networks is a hardware and network-infrastructure vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal or SDK program.

providers.name: Upscale AI
providers.description: Upscale AI is a pure-play AI networking infrastructure company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded by industry veterans from Palo Alto Networks, Marvell, Cisco, and Google and led by CEO Barun Kar. The company builds a full-stack, open-standards AI fabric spanning silicon, systems, and software — its SkyHammer scale-up ASIC architecture and NVIDIA Spectrum-X/SONiC-based scale-out Ethernet systems connect accelerators, memory, and storage for large-scale AI training and inference. Backed by Mayfield among others (Premji Invest, NVIDIA, Salesforce Ventures, Temasek, Tiger Global), it has raised $500M total at a $2B valuation. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface surface beyond a Webflow-served llms.txt; it sells networking hardware and software evaluated by hyperscalers and neoclouds.

providers.name: Lifemote
providers.description: Lifemote Networks is an Istanbul-based provider of AI-driven home Wi-Fi analytics and experience management for broadband ISPs and network operators. A software agent running on the subscriber gateway or access point streams detailed in-home Wi-Fi performance telemetry to Lifemote's cloud, which scores quality of experience per household and per device and isolates root causes such as poor coverage, misplaced repeaters, congested or co-channel Wi-Fi, legacy client devices, and non-Wi-Fi interference. Operators consume the results through a web application for first-line support, proactive maintenance, churn detection and mesh/gateway upselling, plus quarterly expert-reviewed QoE reports. Lifemote markets a full-featured API for integrating this data with in-house OSS/BSS systems and support workflows, but that API is sold and provisioned through direct enterprise engagement — there is no public developer portal, documentation site, machine-readable specification, or self-service sign-up. Customers named publicly include A1, Community Fibre, Online.nl, and Tusass.

providers.name: BTI Systems (Juniper)
providers.description: BTI Systems was an Ottawa, Ontario based supplier of cloud and metro packet-optical networking systems and software, best known for the BTI 7800 Series Packet Optical Transport platform, the BTI 800 Series, and the proNX family of management software (proNX Service Manager and proNX Optical Director). Juniper Networks acquired the remaining ownership interest in BTI Systems for approximately $25.8 million in cash, closing the acquisition on April 1, 2016, to accelerate open and automated packet-optical transport and SDN/NFV capabilities. BTI no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no independent developer portal or public API; the BTI Series and proNX product lines are documented and supported under Juniper Networks, whose proNX Optical Director exposes REST APIs northbound for OSS/BSS integration with NETCONF and telemetry southbound. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network, with the live vendor surface tracked in the juniper-networks profile.

providers.name: Zymbly
providers.description: Zymbly is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a voice-first AI copilot for aircraft maintenance. Its AI agents automate the administrative half of a maintenance technician's day at airlines and MROs (maintenance, repair, and overhaul organizations): troubleshooting issues, looking up parts, retrieving technical documentation, and generating compliant paperwork so technicians can focus on the aircraft. Zymbly is a demo-led B2B product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from the company's public marketing site.

providers.name: Altira Health
providers.description: Altira Health is a San Francisco-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2025, building AI-powered clinical follow-up for health systems. Its virtual clinical assistant, Lena, engages discharged and at-risk patients over voice and SMS, carries clinical context from the EMR across interactions, adapts across languages, escalates to human clinicians when needed, and documents findings directly back into the electronic medical record. The platform aims to recover clinician staff time and reduce hospital readmissions, and advertises API, webhook, dashboard, and analytics surfaces for connected EMR workflows (no public developer portal or API documentation is published as of this profile). Backed by Homebrew, Coalition, Focal, Stone Mountain Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures.

providers.name: CesiumAstro
providers.description: CesiumAstro designs, manufactures, and tests full-stack communication systems and satellites for space, air, and ground missions. The Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, builds active phased array payloads (Vireo), software-defined radios (SDR-1001/2051/2104/3104), reconfigurable processing units, SATCOM terminals (Skylark), tactical ISR/PNT payloads (Nightingale), and the integrated Element LEO satellite platform. Its hardware enables inter-satellite links, high-speed downlinks, lunar communications, and 5G non-terrestrial networks. CesiumAstro publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company as an aerospace hardware provider in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Satellite
providers.description: Satellite IM builds privacy-focused, decentralized peer-to-peer communication software for crypto and web3 communities. Its core is Warp, a Rust interface-driven distributed data service providing end-to-end-encrypted chat, voice, video, and file sharing with data stored on IPFS. Uplink is a customizable decentralized chat application built on top of Warp. Satellite publishes no hosted REST or GraphQL API; the developer surface is the open-source Warp Rust crates and the first-party warp-wasm WebAssembly and TypeScript library. Satellite is backed by Multicoin Capital and its code is MIT licensed.

providers.name: Somos Internet
providers.description: Somos Internet is a Colombian residential and business fiber-optic internet service provider (ISP) delivering high-speed home and enterprise broadband across cities including Medellin, Bogota, Sabaneta, Rionegro, Caldas and Laureles. The company is building AI-ready digital infrastructure for Latin America and raised a $40M Series B backed by Ribbit Capital. It offers fiber internet plans, parental controls, TV channel line-ups, and Wi-Fi routers to homes, businesses, and property developers. No public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or other programmatic surface has been identified for Somos Internet; it is a consumer and enterprise connectivity provider rather than an API platform.

providers.name: TIM
providers.description: TIM S.p.A. (formerly Telecom Italia) is the incumbent Italian telecommunications operator headquartered in Rome and one of the largest telcos in Europe. The group operates fixed and mobile networks across Italy under the TIM Consumer and TIM Enterprise brands, runs TIM Brasil (the second-largest mobile operator in Brazil), and owns a portfolio of technology subsidiaries including Sparkle (international connectivity and quantum-safe infrastructure), Noovle (cloud), Telsy (cybersecurity), and Olivetti (IT services). TIM exposes its mobile network as a programmable platform through the developer.tim.it portal in Italy and through TIM Open Gateway in Brazil, both implementing CAMARA-standard network APIs (SIM Swap, Number Verification, Know Your Customer, IP-to-MSISDN, IP-to- Number, Device Location) jointly defined by the Linux Foundation, TM Forum, and GSMA. These APIs let banks, fintechs, insurers, retailers, and online services authenticate users, detect SIM-swap fraud, verify customer identity, and locate devices using TIM's mobile network as the trust anchor. As of late 2025 TIM Brasil reported 50 million Open Gateway API queries across its catalog.

providers.name: WhatsCookin'
providers.description: WhatsCookin' is a community cooperation platform — a "Cooperation Engine for Communities" — that helps people organize local and virtual gatherings and build healthy social connections. Members join or create Circles (community spaces for conversation and events), post Offers to gauge interest in potential events, and make Wishes that others can fulfill by hosting. Communities span wellness, community-building, language exchange, and food, with active circles in Tucson, Queens, San Francisco, and Oakland. It is available on the web and as native iOS and Android apps. Backed by Bloomberg Beta. There is no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Belden
providers.description: Belden Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets networking, connectivity, and cable products and solutions for industrial automation, smart buildings, and broadcast markets. The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

providers.name: Kodiak Networks
providers.description: Kodiak Networks built a carrier-grade Push-to-Talk over Cellular (PoC) platform that wireless operators deployed as their own branded push-to-talk service, competing with legacy land mobile radio for dispatch, field-service and public-safety workforces. Motorola Solutions acquired the company in 2017 and the technology now ships as Motorola Solutions' "Kodiak" mission-critical push-to-talk (MCPTT) offering for carriers, aligned to the 3GPP SA WG6 MCPTT specifications (TS 23.379, TS 24.382, TS 24.482, TS 22.582) and interoperable with land mobile radio through Critical Connect. Kodiak Networks no longer operates independently: its legacy domain serves only a static "Site under maintenance" placeholder over plain HTTP, and it publishes no OpenAPI, developer documentation, SDKs or public API surface of its own. Broadband push-to-talk APIs for third-party integration do exist, but access is gated behind the Motorola Solutions Application Developer Program.

providers.name: Pensando *
providers.description: AMD Pensando (formerly Pensando Systems, acquired by AMD in 2022) builds programmable Distributed Services Cards (DPUs) and the Policy and Services Manager (PSM) control plane that operates them across cloud, distributed services switch, and enterprise deployments.
