PSM exposes a REST API — surfaced through auto-generated, first-party Python bindings on PyPI (pensando-cloud, pensando-dss, pensando-ent) and a Terraform provider — for managing clusters, networks, security policy, and services on Pensando infrastructure. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Affirmed Networks
providers.description: Affirmed Networks is a mobile networking company founded in 2010 (Andover, Massachusetts) that pioneered fully virtualized, cloud-native mobile core software for service providers. Its portfolio spanned a Virtualized Evolved Packet Core (vEPC), the UnityCloud 5G Core, Private Network Service, Network Slicing, and service-automation/analytics tooling, deployed by 100+ mobile operators including AT&T, Orange, Vodafone, and Telus. The company was acquired by Microsoft in March 2020 and folded into the Azure for Operators initiative; the affirmednetworks.com site now operates as a Microsoft company marketing presence with no independent public developer portal or API. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Axamer
providers.description: Axamer is the company behind Menteo (menteo.ai), an AI-agent platform for restaurants and restaurant chains, focused on Latin America. Menteo deploys a team of specialized AI agents for marketing (WhatsApp and email campaigns), 24/7 WhatsApp order taking, loyalty and rewards programs, and customer service, integrating with existing POS systems, delivery platforms, and messaging channels to unify customer data and automate marketing, sales, and retention. Plans start from $149 USD/month with no long-term contract. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Menteo publishes a public marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy but no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: C2M
providers.description: C2M A.S. is the company behind Connected2.me, a consumer mobile messaging and social application that lets people create a profile, receive messages, and chat in real time with new contacts around the world. The app supports anonymous and identified conversations, following friends, and online-status notifications, and is distributed on both iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play). Connected2.me is a consumer-facing product with no public developer program, API, or SDK surface at this time; its published surface is limited to the marketing site, the mobile apps, and its legal documents (Terms of Service and Privacy Policy). C2M was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: chatous
providers.description: Chatous is a consumer messaging application for random, anonymous chat with real people from around the world over text and video. It connects strangers by shared interests using topic hashtags, letting users make friends and start conversations across iOS and Android. Chatous is a mobile-first social product backed by Slow Ventures; it publishes a consumer website, privacy policy, and terms of service but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documented API program at this time.

providers.name: Crown Castle
providers.description: Crown Castle is a leading United States provider of shared communications infrastructure including cell towers, small cells, and fiber. Crown Castle owns and operates more than 40,000 cell towers and approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber, supporting wireless carriers, enterprises, and government customers with managed connectivity, dark fiber, optical encryption, ultra-low-latency transport, and managed SD-WAN services. Crown Castle does not currently publish a public developer API program; technical integrations are handled through customer and channel partner agreements.

providers.name: Dialup
providers.description: Dialup is a voice-chat app that revives the magic of talking on the phone by pairing people for one-on-one calls based on shared interests. It automates recurring, scheduled calls so users connect serendipitously with friends, communities, or complete strangers around the world without any manual coordination. Callers opt in with custom caller IDs rather than random numbers, and the free service is available on iOS and Android. Dialup is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it operates as a consumer social/communication application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Jarvie
providers.description: Jarvie is a consumer AI assistant from All Day Technologies, Inc. that lives inside iMessage and SMS group chats. Marketed as "your group chat sidekick," it helps people who text together plan events, learn things, and have fun, and can draft emails and create calendar events on a user's behalf. It offers memory features to personalize responses across conversations. Jarvie is a mobile-messaging consumer product surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; as of this profile it does not publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rakuten Mobile
providers.description: Rakuten Mobile is the Japanese mobile network operator (MNO) of Rakuten Group, headquartered in Setagaya, Tokyo, and Japan's fourth nationwide carrier alongside NTT Docomo, KDDI, and SoftBank. Commercially launched in April 2020 and surpassing 10 million subscribers in December 2025, Rakuten Mobile built and operates the world's first fully cloud-native, end-to-end virtualized mobile network on Open RAN, with 4G population coverage of 99.9% and expanding 5G plus 700 MHz Platinum Band rollout. The same engineering effort spun out into Rakuten Symphony, a B2B business that productizes the Rakuten Mobile playbook as the Symworld platform — a cloud-native operating platform for telcos covering Open RAN (CU/DU/RIC, Symware distributed unit appliance), Symworld Cloud (Kubernetes-based hyperconverged telco cloud / CNP), OSS/BSS, site management, and a marketplace of pre-integrated cloud-native network functions from 50+ vendor partners. Symphony also offers Rakuten CPaaS (carrier-grade SMS, Confirm/OTP, and Short URL APIs running on the Rakuten Mobile network with JWT-authenticated REST endpoints at api.cpaas.symphony.rakuten.net) and Rakuten Communications Platform (RCP) for enterprise private 5G. Public, developer-accessible APIs are concentrated in the CPaaS suite; the Symworld platform APIs themselves are TM Forum-aligned but exposed under commercial engagement rather than a public developer signup.

providers.name: Tejas Networks
providers.description: Tejas Networks is an India-based telecommunications networking products company (part of the Tata group) that designs and manufactures a wall-to-wall portfolio of wireline and wireless networking equipment for telecom carriers, internet service providers, utilities, defense, and governments. Its product lines span Radio Access Network (4G/5G RAN), fiber broadband access (FTTx/GPON), packet-optical and DWDM/OTN transport (TJ1600), converged broadband (TJ1400), switching and routing, mobile packet core, satcom, and Direct-to-Mobile broadcast, all managed through the TejNMS (TJ5500) network management system. Tejas exposes an EMS/NMS management API for its equipment, but that interface and its product documentation are delivered through a login-gated customer documentation library rather than a public developer program; there is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: AlgoX2
providers.description: AlgoX2 is a data streaming operating system that unifies ingestion, ordering, fan-out, transformation, and durable storage into a single fault-tolerant engine, positioned as an alternative to assembling Kafka, Flink, and Redis. Built by veterans of NYSE Pillar's matching engine, the platform offers a partition-free API, compute-storage separation, a zero-copy runtime, and native multicast fan-out, with native support for Kafka, NATS, MQTT, Redis, HTTP, and WebSocket protocols and protocol bridging between them. Streams automatically materialize as Apache Iceberg, Delta, or Hudi tables in S3-compatible Parquet storage for lakehouse integration. AlgoX2 raised a $3.5M seed round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and serves real-time use cases including exchange and matching-engine infrastructure, market-data distribution, risk and surveillance, backtesting, and AI feature streaming.

providers.name: Apparta
providers.description: Apparta is a Colombian hospitality technology company providing a reservation-management and guest-engagement platform for restaurants, bars, and dining venues across Latin America (Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla). The SaaS product covers AI-assisted table assignment and floor-plan zoning, no-show prevention with prepayments and cancellation policies, a WhatsApp AI chatbot for automated bookings, CRM campaigns over SMS/email/WhatsApp, POS integration, branded booking pages and digital menus, and marketing connectors to Google, Google Maps, Instagram, TripAdvisor, and Facebook. Apparta is offered in tiered monthly plans (Basico, Standard, Plus) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profiling; higher tiers expose a WhatsApp Business API integration on behalf of venues rather than a first-party Apparta API.

providers.name: Raseedi
providers.description: Raseedi is an Egyptian financial technology platform that helps underbanked users manage their spending and save money. Through its mobile app it offers free and discounted calls, mobile top-ups and bill payments, cash loans, and a smart dialer, building a community for financial control and savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Raseedi runs a Wix-hosted marketing site with no first-party developer API; its only machine-readable surface is a published llms.txt and the generic Wix Site MCP endpoint.

providers.name: Movandi
providers.description: Movandi is an RF semiconductor company founded by former Broadcom executives (CEO Maryam Rofougaran and CTO Reza Rofougaran) that designs 5G mmWave chipsets, RF front ends, phased-array antenna modules, 5G smart repeaters, and beamforming software for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Based in Irvine, California and backed by Sierra Ventures, the company holds 130+ patents covering millimeter wave semiconductor, system, and software technologies spanning 5G, fixed wireless, and satellite connectivity. Movandi is a hardware/semiconductor vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Boardy
providers.description: Boardy is an AI networking agent — an "AI Superconnector" that facilitates meaningful professional introductions. Users message Boardy (via chat and voice) to describe who they want to meet, and it matches them with relevant people from its network, sharing contact details only after both parties explicitly opt in to connect. Boardy is a free consumer product backed by Creandum; it uses public LinkedIn profile information to facilitate introductions and documents its data handling in a GDPR-aligned privacy policy and terms of service. Boardy publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time — its public surface is a marketing site, legal pages, and an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Level AI
providers.description: Level AI (legally Ujwal Inc.) is a Mountain View, California contact center AI company founded in 2019 by Ashish Nagar, a former member of Amazon's Alexa conversational AI team. The company builds LLM-native customer experience intelligence and service automation for enterprise contact centers, with a platform spanning two product surfaces: a CX Delivery suite (AI Virtual Agent, Agent Assist, AgentGPT, Coaching, Manager Assist, Knowledge Bot, Auto Summary, Agent Screen Recording) and a CX Strategy suite (Auto-QA on 100% of interactions, Voice of the Customer theme detection, omnichannel Analytics, iCSAT, AI Workers). The proprietary full-stack AI platform includes Level AI's own ASR/Voice AI and semantic-intelligence layer trained on customer-service data, and is positioned for financial services, insurance, healthcare, retail, banking, and collections operations. Level AI exposes a public REST API for bidirectional data exchange with BI tools and existing contact center stacks, and ships native integrations across telephony, CRM, customer support, workforce management, CX management, communication, learning management, and SSO categories. The company has raised $73.1M to date (Series A 2021, Series B 2022 led by Battery Ventures, Series C $39.4M 2024 led by Adams Street Partners with Cross Creek, Brightloop, Battery Ventures and Eniac Ventures), holds a 4.7/5 rating on G2, and reports customer outcomes including 25% CSAT lift, 45% agent satisfaction improvement, and 90% time savings on manual QA. The Level AI GitHub organization (github.com/Level-AI) exists but is currently empty — there is no public OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source release; the API is documented and credentialed through the customer's tenant of the Level AI platform.

providers.name: Polycom
providers.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cohere Technologies
providers.description: Cohere Technologies is a San Jose, California wireless communications software company developing spectral-efficiency technology for mobile networks. Its Universal Spectrum Multiplier (USM) software delivers a 2x spectrum multiplier for 4G, 5G, and Multi-G networks across FDD and TDD bands, and its Pulsone technology applies the Zak-OTFS (Orthogonal Time Frequency Space) waveform to Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) and Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). The company sells to mobile network operators and Open RAN ecosystems and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, NEA, Telstra Ventures, Intel Capital, Koch Investments Group, VMware, and Juniper Networks. Cohere Technologies is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: i2x
providers.description: i2x is a German real-time AI platform for contact centers, built by i2x GmbH in Mönchengladbach. It provides live agent assistance that surfaces contextual recommendations during calls in under 0.4 seconds, including automatic detection of purchase signals and faster agent onboarding; full-coverage call analysis with automatic transcription plus quality, compliance, and sales-opportunity scoring across 100% of conversations; and voicebots for automated inbound/outbound telephony and virtual agent-training scenarios. The platform emphasizes DSGVO/GDPR compliance with EU-only hosting in German data centers, prepared works-council documentation, and EU AI Act alignment, positioning itself as an alternative to US-cloud-dependent conversation-intelligence tools. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are currently published; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hv-capital.

providers.name: Skylo
providers.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

providers.name: Volterra
providers.description: Volterra was a Santa Clara-based distributed cloud company founded in 2017 by Ankur Singla, Harshad Nakil, and Ashish Ranjan, offering the VoltMesh (multi-cloud networking and security) and VoltStack (edge application deployment) SaaS platforms on a global application delivery network. Backed by roughly $50M from Khosla Ventures, Mayfield, M12, Samsung NEXT, and Itochu Technology Ventures, Volterra was acquired by F5 in January 2021 for approximately $500M and became the foundation of F5 Distributed Cloud Services. Its API surface (ves.io.schema, console.ves.volterra.io) is catalogued in the F5 Distributed Cloud Services profile, while the Volterra-branded Terraform provider and vesctl CLI remain published and maintained by F5.

providers.name: Nexiu
providers.description: Nexiu (Nexiu AI LLC) is a Latin America-focused recruiting automation platform that uses AI agents to source, contact, screen, and schedule high-volume candidates over the official WhatsApp Business API, integrating with Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Meet) and existing ATS systems and job boards. It offers a fully managed pay-per-hire service (Nexiu Managed) and a self-service SaaS platform (Nexiu Platform) for internal talent-acquisition teams, and is backed by 500 Global (500 Latam) and NVIDIA Inception. As of this pass Nexiu consumes third-party APIs (WhatsApp Business, Google, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

providers.name: Brunswick Corporation
providers.description: Brunswick Corporation is a global leader in marine recreation and technology, headquartered in Mettawa, Illinois (NYSE: BC). Brunswick owns over 60 brands across marine propulsion (Mercury Marine, Mercury Racing, MerCruiser, Fliteboard), boat manufacturing (Boston Whaler, Sea Ray, Bayliner, Lund, Crestliner, Harris, Lowe, heyday), and marine parts and accessories (Navico Group: B&G, C-Map, Lowrance, Simrad). The company's ACES innovation strategy centers on Autonomy/Assistance, Connectivity, Electrification, and Shared Access.

providers.name: Convergys
providers.description: Convergys was a global leader in customer management services, providing customer care, technology services, and analytics across industries before being acquired by Concentrix in October 2018. The legacy convergys.com domain now redirects to Concentrix, and Convergys offerings such as contact center outsourcing, workforce management, analytics, and digital customer experience platforms have been folded into the Concentrix portfolio. Concentrix itself does not publish public REST APIs or developer programs in the way SaaS vendors do. Most platform integrations are delivered through enterprise contracts and private APIs.

providers.name: Once
providers.description: Once (getonce.com) is a consumer chat and connection platform positioned as an alternative to traditional dating apps, offering a pressure-free space for people seeking meaningful connections, improved social skills, and guidance in their personal lives. The mobile app surfaces a small number of daily matches based on shared interests and vibes, lets users join communities of like-minded people, and runs a rewards system called Sparks that members earn and spend on gifts and chat features. Once is a Consumer-sector portfolio company of the venture firm Partech. It ships as a consumer mobile application and does not currently expose a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Aliro Quantum
providers.description: Aliro Quantum (branded "Aliro, The Quantum Networking Company") is a Boston-based, Harvard spin-out building full-stack software for entanglement-based quantum networks. Its platform unifies three core products: the Aliro Simulator for physically accurate, optical-level modeling and validation of heterogeneous quantum networks before any hardware is deployed; AlirOS, a vendor-agnostic control-plane operating system that runs on quantum end-nodes and quantum repeaters across multiple hardware modalities; and the Aliro Orchestrator, a centralized single-pane-of-glass management system that configures, monitors, and operates quantum nodes and services through the full network lifecycle. These are packaged commercially as AliroNet — described by Aliro as the world's first end-to-end entanglement-based quantum network solution — delivered in three modes (Emulate, Pilot, and Deployment) and also available as AliroNet Quickstart, a bundled hardware-plus-software starter package that pairs third-party photon sources, detectors, memories, repeaters, and routers with Aliro's orchestration, control, and data operations software. The company markets Quantum-Powered Security as its anchor use case (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation for telcos, utilities, financial services, and defense), alongside quantum-computing interconnects (clustered and blind quantum compute for cloud providers), networked quantum sensors for positioning/navigation/timing, and quantum position verification. Customers and design partners disclosed publicly include EPB of Chattanooga, Boeing, Cisco, the US Air Force, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Stony Brook University, and Noblis. Aliro is backed by deep-tech investors including Cisco Investments and Accenture Ventures, reports more than 50 third-party quantum networking devices already integrated with its stack, and operates with hardware-agnostic positioning across photonic, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and diamond-defect node technologies. There is no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or open-source repository — the AlirOS APIs referenced in Aliro's product materials are vendor-facing integration interfaces consumed under commercial engagement, and Aliro's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: clounix
providers.description: Clounix (云合智网, Yunhe Zhiwang) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Shanghai, with additional offices in Hangzhou, Nanjing, Beijing, and Chengdu. It designs high-end networking and communication silicon — high-performance programmable Ethernet switch chips, DPUs (Data Processing Units), and SmartNIC intelligent network cards — along with cloud-native infrastructure hardware and customized software for data centers and 5G networks. Its switch platforms run the open-source SONiC network operating system, and the company maintains a public GitHub organization with SONiC/SAI networking software. Clounix is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It currently publishes no public developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Cablevision Systems
providers.description: Cablevision Systems was a U.S. cable television company that provided telecommunications and television services (Optimum TV, Optimum Online, Optimum Voice) in the New York metropolitan area. It was acquired by Altice in 2016 and now operates as part of Altice USA under the Optimum consumer brand.

providers.name: CRM Bonus
providers.description: CRM Bonus (CRMBonus) is a Brazilian retail technology platform for customer acquisition, conversion, and loyalty. Its products include Giftback cashback and rewards, the Vale Bonus consumer rewards app connecting brands to over five million shoppers, CRMBack WhatsApp-based e-commerce conversion, and CRMAds retail media on WhatsApp. It integrates with 300+ ERP, point-of-sale, and e-commerce systems including VTEX, Shopify, Linx, TOTVS, Nuvemshop, and PagSeguro. Integration is delivered through partner connectors rather than a public developer API; no public API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Astranis
providers.description: Astranis designs, manufactures, and operates small, dedicated geostationary communications satellites known as MicroGEO. Each spacecraft uses radiation-hardened digital payload technology to deliver dedicated broadband capacity to specific countries, telecom operators, enterprise users, and the U.S. government. Astranis is a satellite operator and manufacturer rather than an API provider; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: IKANO Communications
providers.description: IKANO Communications, Inc. is a diversified consumer and business Internet company founded in 1999 and headquartered in metropolitan Los Angeles, with additional offices in Salt Lake City and Toronto, Canada. IKANO provides hosted voice services and broadband Internet access through direct and wholesale/private-label channels. Its primary brands include Broadvoice, a provider of feature-rich broadband phone (VoIP) service to consumers and businesses across the continental US and Canada, and DSL Extreme, a provider of high-speed and traditional Internet access. IKANO is a wholly owned subsidiary of Teutonic Holdings, LLC. The company publishes a marketing and corporate site only; it exposes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface at this time.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Pivotal Commware
providers.description: Pivotal Commware develops millimeter wave (mmWave) infrastructure for 5G networks, built around its Holographic Beam Forming technology and what it calls the world's first smart repeater ecosystem. Its product line includes WaveScape network-planning software, the Pivot 5G outdoor network repeater, the Echo 5G subscriber repeater for indoor mmWave coverage, and IBMS, an Intelligent Beam Management System that pairs machine learning with smart repeaters for real-time network optimization. The company is venture-backed by Lux Capital. As of this enrichment pass Pivotal Commware publishes a corporate and marketing site (datasheets, white papers, videos, and a blog) but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: Per Vices
providers.description: Per Vices Corporation is a Toronto-based company that designs and manufactures high-performance software defined radio (SDR) platforms, where signal tuning is handled in hardware while the remaining radio functionality runs in software so a single application-agnostic platform can serve many markets. Its product line includes Cyan (up to 16 independent radio chains, near-DC to 18 GHz), Crimson TNG (4 Rx / 4 Tx, near-DC to 6 GHz), Chestnut (near-DC to 9 GHz on an Intel Stratix 10 FPGA), and Calamine (receive-only, near-DC to 40 GHz). Per Vices ships open-source host software and firmware built on the UHD (USRP Hardware Driver) framework rather than a public web API; developers program the radios through the UHD C++ driver, GNU Radio integration, and example applications published on its GitHub org, with full integration support provided directly to customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with company identity and a security probe; it publishes no public REST/OpenAPI web API surface.

providers.name: Piris Labs
providers.description: Piris Labs is a Y Combinator (W2026) deep-tech startup building the networking layer for AI. The company develops proprietary photonic interconnect technology paired with a vertically optimized software stack that moves data between AI accelerators at ultra-low latency, targeting the bottleneck where up to 80% of advanced AI compute sits idle waiting on slow networking. Piris Labs couples this optical fabric with a full-stack, low-latency inference offering and has reported some of the fastest inference speeds for large frontier models. Founded in San Francisco by Ali Khalatpour (CEO) and Keyvan Moghadam (President), the company currently exposes no public, documented developer API or SDK — its product is delivered as hardware plus a hosted inference stack behind an early-access waitlist. This profile tracks Piris Labs' identity in the API Evangelist network and any future API surface it publishes.

providers.name: QMC
providers.description: QMC Telecom is a provider of shared telecommunications infrastructure for mobile networks, operating across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and Chile. The company develops, owns, operates, and leases indoor connectivity solutions, street-level solutions (SLS), and towers, rooftops, and special sites, positioning itself as a partner in 5G network densification. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this is a hardware and telecommunications-infrastructure company that publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Shenandoah Telecommunications
providers.description: Shenandoah Telecommunications Company (SHEN), doing business as Shentel, is a publicly traded telecommunications company headquartered in Edinburg, Virginia. For over 100 years, Shentel has provided internet, TV, and phone services to residential and business customers across Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Delaware, Ohio, and Indiana. The company operates a digital wireless and wireline network delivering broadband internet, video, and voice services. Through its Glo Fiber and Glo Fiber Business brands, Shentel provides high-speed fiber optic internet, Ethernet, wavelength services, managed network services, and dark fiber leasing to enterprise and wholesale customers. Shentel operates approximately 15,400 route miles of fiber on a MEF-certified network, with connectivity including the Washington D.C. market via CoreSite.

providers.name: Bug Labs
providers.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

providers.name: Voxeet
providers.description: Voxeet was a San Francisco-based startup that built spatial-audio voice and video conferencing APIs and SDKs for web and mobile applications, backed by 500 Global. Dolby Laboratories acquired Voxeet in 2019 and rebranded its technology as the Dolby.io Communications APIs and SDKs. That surface has since been retired -- the voxeet GitHub org archived all 88 repositories on 2024-08-30 and the Dolby.io Communications documentation now redirects to Dolby OptiView. This profile preserves the historical record; see the dolby and dolby-io profiles for the successor platform.

providers.name: AVI Networks
providers.description: AVI Networks builds a software-defined application delivery platform - the Avi Vantage Platform / Avi Load Balancer - providing multi-cloud load balancing, web application firewall (WAF), GSLB, container ingress, and analytics driven by a central Avi Controller with a fully programmable REST API. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, AVI Networks was acquired by VMware in 2019 and the product is now offered by Broadcom as the VMware Avi Load Balancer. The controller exposes a comprehensive REST API with first-party Python, Go, and Java SDKs, a Terraform provider, and Ansible automation for intent-based, self-service application services across VMware, AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, and bare-metal environments.

providers.name: eBPF
providers.description: eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) is a technology that allows programs to run in a sandboxed virtual machine within the Linux kernel without changing kernel source code or loading kernel modules. It enables high-performance networking, security monitoring, observability, and tracing capabilities at the operating system level with minimal overhead. eBPF is governed as a standard by the eBPF Foundation under the Linux Foundation.

providers.name: Sonus
providers.description: Sonus is the API Evangelist network profile for the company that began as Sonus Networks, an early pioneer of VoIP softswitches and session border controllers (SBCs), and which today operates as Ribbon Communications (NASDAQ: RBBN) following its 2017 merger with GENBAND. Ribbon builds real-time communications, IP optical networking, session border control, cloud and edge, and network security and analytics software for service providers and enterprises. This profile originated as a Matrix Partners portfolio lead. Ribbon publishes enterprise product, support, and responsible-disclosure resources but no public developer API or open API specification was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Geneva
providers.description: Geneva is an all-in-one communication app for groups, clubs, and communities — "the online place to find your offline people." It bundles full-featured group chat (threaded replies, reactions, GIFs, attachments, polls, pins), audio/video rooms and livestreaming for hundreds of viewers, event planning, and wallet-connect with token-gated rooms for tokenized communities. Geneva ships as free iOS, Android, and web apps and was acquired by Bumble Inc. This API Evangelist profile entered the network as a VC-portfolio-sourced stub; the company publishes a consumer app with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Key
providers.description: Key AI is a professional networking platform that rebuilds business connection-making around AI and consent-based introductions. Its Kai AI agent surfaces the right people through warm paths in your existing network, while Handshake handles consent-first introductions (launching summer 2026). The platform also offers matched Opportunities (jobs, deals, and partnerships), branded Communities and directories for alumni groups and associations, event and calendar pre-matching, a searchable knowledge Library, and Connectors for Slack, WhatsApp, and LinkedIn. Founded by Google alumni behind the 35,000-member Xoogler community and backed by Felicis, Key AI is an end-user and community-operator product; as of July 2026 it publishes no public API, developer platform, or API documentation.

providers.name: Letel
providers.description: Shanghai Letel Communication Equipment (Group) Co., Ltd. (上海乐通通信设备（集团）股份有限公司) is a Chinese manufacturer of information and communication network infrastructure, founded in March 1992 and headquartered in Shanghai with over 1,500 employees and 20+ service locations nationwide. Letel builds data center physical infrastructure — cabinet micromodules, cold aisle micromodules, containerized micromodules, pallet IT cabins, and cabinets — alongside communication cabling equipment, optical communication devices, data communication equipment, broadband access equipment, and structural components for notebooks and servers. It operates through subsidiaries including Zhongle Communication Technology Co., Ltd. Letel publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: BAYCON
providers.description: BAYCON Inc. is a Seoul, South Korea-based mobile connectivity company, founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global and Shorooq Partners (seed round, 2024). BAYCON operates a global data eSIM platform and a family of international communication apps: eSIM Easy (이심이지), which delivers multi-country data eSIM plans as a QR code within minutes of purchase; ModuCall (모두의 국제전화), affordable VoIP international calling that lets users place overseas calls using their domestic mobile plans; and BayTalk. The company partners with local network operators and global carrier infrastructure so international travelers and businesses can access local mobile networks without physical SIM cards, cut roaming costs, and stay connected across borders, and is expanding into travel content such as attraction tickets and transportation passes. BAYCON publishes consumer mobile apps rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Occamnetworks
providers.description: Occam Networks was a broadband access equipment vendor that developed and marketed systems enabling telecommunications carriers to profitably deliver emerging voice, video, and high-speed data (triple-play) services over copper and fiber, including its BLC 6000 access platform and ONT/ONU customer-premises hardware. The company was acquired by Calix in early 2011 and no longer operates independently. The occamnetworks.com domain currently serves an archived circa-2010 marketing site (products, solutions, support, news, whitepapers) with no developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Enrichment found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Liveprofile
providers.description: LiveProfile is a cross-platform mobile messaging and chat product ("Stay connected with people and things that matter. Chat securely and express yourself freely."). It was originally backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-derived company profile. As of this enrichment pass, liveprofile.com is an invite-only relaunch teaser ("The New LiveProfile") running a waitlist, with apps advertised for Android, iPhone & iPad, and Mac/PC. The company maintains a public GitHub organization and a BetterUptime status page, but publishes no public API surface, developer documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time — so this profile carries identity and operational signals only, awaiting a real developer/API surface.

providers.name: HUM Industries
providers.description: HUM Industries is a consumer hardware company building a wearable AI assistant designed to enhance social presence. The device records conversations locally, maintains a rolling buffer of recent audio, and surfaces contextual information such as names, personal details, and commitments back to the wearer through subtle audio cues. The company frames the product as giving people "the freedom to forget" by offloading memory to the device so they can stay present in the moment. At the time of profiling the product is pre-launch, offered through a preorder waitlist, with no public API, developer portal, or third-party integration surface. Backed by a16z; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Enterprise Integration Patterns
providers.description: Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP) is a catalog of architectural design patterns for integrating enterprise applications. The patterns describe messaging-based integration scenarios and provide a common vocabulary for architects and developers to design and implement integration solutions. The canonical reference is the book by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, organized into six pattern categories: Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

providers.name: KDDI
providers.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure. In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

providers.name: Lynq
providers.description: Lynq Networks develops infrastructure-free, long-range wireless connectivity for enterprise and OEM devices, bridging the gap between short-range Bluetooth and infrastructure-dependent cellular/5G. Its technology lets original equipment manufacturers build large-area device networks without deploying traditional network infrastructure, targeting construction, agriculture, military, and public-safety use cases. Lynq is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northwood Space
providers.description: Northwood Space is an El Segundo, California ground-infrastructure company for the space industry, founded in 2022 by Bridgit Mendler (CEO), Griffin Cleverly (CTO), and Shaurya Luthra. It designs and delivers rapidly deployable satellite ground stations built on electronically steerable phased-array antennas that track many satellites at once with no moving parts, paired with software ("Portal") that orchestrates every contact, automates scheduling, and moves data from spacecraft to customer. Northwood aims to turn ground infrastructure into cloud-like, on-demand global capacity for defense and commercial operators. The company's software stack is described as developer-oriented with modern APIs and integration hooks, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Founders Fund, Washington Harbour Partners, and Alpine Space Ventures; raised a $100M Series B and won a $50M Space Force contract in early 2026.

providers.name: Rcom
providers.description: Rcom (Reliance Communications, RCOM) is an Indian telecommunications and digital infrastructure company providing enterprise connectivity, voice, and data-center services. Its portfolio spans dedicated internet access and DDoS protection, IP transit, MPLS VPN, Ethernet and leased lines, cloud networking (Cloud X Fusion / Cloud X WAN), enterprise voice (E1 PRI, SIP trunk, IP Centrex), cloud telephony and hosted contact centers, toll-free and global access numbers, audio/web conferencing, colocation and managed data-center services, and global subsea cable networks via its Global Cloud Xchange subsidiary. The company surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment confirms an enterprise service business with customer and billing portals but no public developer program, API surface, or well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Barefoot Networks
providers.description: Barefoot Networks was a computer-networking company founded in 2013 in Santa Clara, California, that designed and produced programmable network-switch silicon, systems, and software. Its flagship Tofino Intelligent Fabric Processor was the first end-user-programmable Ethernet switch ASIC, built on the Protocol Independent Switch Architecture (PISA) and programmed with the P4 language at line rates up to 12.8 Tbit/s. Developer tooling spanned the P4 Studio SDK, the Barefoot Runtime Interface (BRI) control-plane API, and the Tofino Native Architecture (TNA). Intel acquired Barefoot Networks in June 2019, folding the technology into Intel Tofino / Intel Intelligent Fabric Processors; the barefootnetworks.com corporate site now redirects into Intel, and the surviving open documentation lives in the barefootnetworks GitHub organization (notably the Open-Tofino repository publishing the public TNA and P4 architecture docs).

providers.name: Cumulus Networks
providers.description: Cumulus Networks was a computer networking company founded in 2010 that developed Cumulus Linux, an open Linux-based network operating system for bare-metal and white-box data-center switches, along with NetQ, a network operations and telemetry platform. It was a pioneer of open, disaggregated networking, letting operators run a standard Linux distribution on commodity switching hardware. NVIDIA acquired Cumulus Networks in May 2020, and the products are now part of NVIDIA's Ethernet switching and networking software line. The former cumulusnetworks.com and docs.cumulusnetworks.com domains now redirect to NVIDIA's networking documentation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, Battery Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Interlink
providers.description: interLink is an abstraction layer that extends the Kubernetes Virtual Kubelet interface, enabling pods to execute on remote resources such as HPC batch systems (SLURM, HTCondor), virtual machines, remote Kubernetes clusters, and serverless platforms. It comprises a Virtual Kubelet that converts pod execution requests into remote API calls and a modular interLink API Server with provider-specific sidecar plugins, with built-in OpenTelemetry observability, TLS/mTLS, and OAuth2 authentication.

providers.name: Byanat
providers.description: Byanat is an Oman-based, award-winning AI company offering a unified platform for optimizing digital infrastructure across telecommunications networks and data centers. The platform pairs system-wide visibility with custom-tailored automation to scale operations, ensure compliance, and promote sustainability, an approach the company frames as "Infrastructure 4.0." Its product families span mobile network solutions (site management, degradation detection, auto-discovery, performance analytics), data centre solutions (predictive analytics, capacity forecasting, energy management, infrastructure monitoring), and an API and integration layer for cross-platform connectivity and AI-powered workflow automation. Byanat is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference; its API and integration capability is delivered as a managed product.

providers.name: Hyro
providers.description: Hyro is a responsible AI-powered conversational and agentic communications platform, best known for deploying AI assistants and voice/chat agents for large healthcare systems as well as other regulated enterprises. Its platform automates patient and customer engagement across web, SMS, and voice channels — handling tasks such as appointment management, IT help-desk requests, call routing, and answering high-volume repetitive questions — using a knowledge-graph-driven natural language engine positioned around explainability and control. Hyro is headquartered in New York and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. At enrichment time Hyro exposes no public developer API or OpenAPI specification; its public technical surface consists of a customer product dashboard (docs.hyro.ai) and a live operational status page (status.hyro.ai). This profile was surfaced from the Norwest portfolio and enriched from verifiable public signals only.

providers.name: Kik (Kin)
providers.description: Kik (Kin) refers to the Kin cryptocurrency created by Kik Interactive, the messaging company, as a blockchain-based digital currency for use inside consumer applications. Kin originally launched on a fork of the Stellar network and later migrated to Solana, shipping first-party developer SDKs (JavaScript/Node and Python) under the kinecosystem GitHub organization and a developer program at developer.kin.org. The Kin project is now defunct: the developer surface no longer resolves, every kinecosystem repository is archived, the published SDKs are deprecated, and Kik itself was acquired by MediaLab AI Inc. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and is retained as a historical record of a wound-down crypto developer surface.

providers.name: ToyTalk
providers.description: ToyTalk was a San Francisco conversational AI company founded in 2011 that built voice and chat characters for entertainment, rebranded as PullString in 2016, and was acquired by Apple in early 2019. Its developer platform - the PullString Web API plus Converse and Author tooling for authoring conversational experiences - was shut down after the acquisition. Today pullstring.com and toytalk.com no longer resolve and both domains are parked on Apple nameservers, the github.com/pullstring organization has been deleted, and the only surviving first-party developer artifact is the orphaned pullstring JavaScript SDK on npm. This profile records that historical developer surface; there is no live API.

providers.name: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (JASDAQ:3754)
providers.description: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (エキサイト株式会社), listed on JASDAQ as ticker 3754, is a Tokyo-based internet media and services company founded in August 1997 and headquartered in the Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower in Minato, Tokyo. It operates the long-running excite.co.jp web portal — offering web, image, and news search, the Excite Blog (exblog.jp) blogging platform, translation and dictionary tools, fortune-telling, recipe, and lifestyle content — alongside the BB.excite broadband/ISP business. Under parent Excite Holdings Co., Ltd., the group organizes its operations into four segments: Platform, Broadband, Medical, and SaaS/DX (including the FanGrowth customer-growth platform). The company does not currently publish a public developer API program or portal; this profile tracks its corporate and web presence within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: The Cru
providers.description: The Cru (now branded "The Cru Empowered by Luminary") is a membership community founded by Tiffany Dufu that matches women and allies into small peer-coaching accountability circles ("Crus") of 6-8 members who meet in monthly 90-minute gatherings to advance their personal and professional goals. It was acquired by Luminary, a New York City based professional community and coworking organization, and the thecru.com site now redirects to weareluminary.com/luminary-crus. This is a consumer community and coaching business, not a technical platform - it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: HTTP/2
providers.description: HTTP/2 is the second major version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, defined by the IETF in RFC 7540 and standardized in 2015. It optimizes use of network resources and reduces perceived latency by introducing a binary framing layer over a single TCP connection, with full request and response multiplexing across independent bidirectional streams. HTTP/2 uses HPACK header compression to eliminate redundant header data, credit-based flow control via WINDOW_UPDATE frames, stream prioritization through dependencies and weights, and server push via PUSH_PROMISE frames to proactively deliver anticipated resources. Core frame types include DATA, HEADERS, PRIORITY, RST_STREAM, SETTINGS, PUSH_PROMISE, PING, and GOAWAY, with the protocol preserving the existing HTTP semantics of methods, status codes, and headers while transforming how they are transported on the wire.

providers.name: Streamroot
providers.description: Streamroot was a Paris-founded video-delivery company (backed by Partech and Techstars) that built a peer-to-peer / multi-CDN "Mesh Delivery" and DNA SDK to offload live and on-demand video traffic onto a hybrid CDN+WebRTC peer mesh, reducing bandwidth cost and improving scale for broadcasters and OTT platforms. The developer surface was a client-side (browser and native player) delivery SDK distributed as video-player plugins (video.js, Clappr, hls.js, AVPlayer) rather than a server-side REST API. Streamroot was acquired by CenturyLink — now Lumen Technologies — in 2019 and folded into Lumen's CDN / Mesh Delivery product line. The standalone streamroot.io website and developer docs are offline; the surviving public assets are the (now Lumen-operated) GitHub organization and a set of official but deprecated npm player-plugin packages.

providers.name: Xirrus
providers.description: Xirrus was an enterprise Wi-Fi company that made high-density wireless access points and arrays managed through the Xirrus Management System (XMS), which exposed a management API that community client libraries were built against. Backed by Canaan Partners, Xirrus was acquired by Riverbed Technology in April 2017 to power cloud-managed Wi-Fi in SteelConnect, and Riverbed sold the Xirrus Wi-Fi business to Cambium Networks in 2019. The Xirrus brand has since been absorbed into Cambium Networks' enterprise Wi-Fi portfolio, and xirrus.com now redirects to cambiumnetworks.com, leaving no independent Xirrus API surface.

providers.name: Aerohive
providers.description: Aerohive Networks was a cloud-managed networking company founded in 2006 by Changming Liu and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It pioneered controller-less, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and edge networking, managed through its HiveManager NG (later ExtremeCloud IQ) platform and access points. Aerohive went public on the NYSE under the ticker HIVE and was acquired by Extreme Networks in a deal that closed on 2019-08-09 for approximately $272 million. The company operated an Aerohive Developer Program with a public developer portal (developer.aerohive.com) and REST APIs for the HiveManager NG / ACS platform, plus a GitHub organization of reference applications. Following the acquisition the products were folded into ExtremeCloud IQ, and the legacy Aerohive API and its developer portal were retired (shutdown dated 2026-07-12), with integrators directed to migrate to the Extreme Platform ONE Developer Portal. This profile enriches the historical Aerohive API surface; it is a retired/acquired provider.

providers.name: Edgeware
providers.description: Edgeware AB was a Swedish video-delivery technology company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Stockholm, known for its TV CDN, origin and media server, and streaming video-delivery products used by telecom operators and broadcasters to run OTT and IPTV services. Backed by Creandum, it listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2016 and was acquired by Agile Content (Agile Content S.A.) in 2020. The Edgeware brand has since been consolidated into AgileTV: edgeware.tv now redirects to agiletv.com/edgeware/, and its developer/technical documentation lives under docs.agilecontent.com (AgileTV Origin & Media Server, CDN Solutions, Subtitling). Edgeware no longer operates as an independent company or publishes an independent developer API surface.

providers.name: Rfmd
providers.description: RFMD (RF Micro Devices) was a semiconductor manufacturer of radio-frequency (RF) components for mobile, infrastructure, defense, and aerospace markets. In January 2015 RFMD merged with TriQuint Semiconductor to form Qorvo, and the rfmd.com domain now redirects to qorvo.com. Qorvo designs and manufactures RF and power solutions — amplifiers, filters, integrated circuits, wireless connectivity, and power management devices — spanning mobile, defense/aerospace, network infrastructure, IoT, automotive, and consumer electronics. As a hardware semiconductor company, RFMD/Qorvo publishes no public developer web API; its developer-facing resources are simulation models, QSPICE circuit-simulation software, datasheets, evaluation boards, and a technical support forum. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners and enriched to reflect the RFMD-to-Qorvo identity; there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Tsumobi
providers.description: Tsumobi was a Y Combinator (Winter 2007) mobile messaging startup founded in Boston by Joshua Wilson and Adam Bouhenguel, and later backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It built a programming language that sat on top of J2ME so feature-phone applications could be downloaded and updated on the fly via URLs, aiming to fix the painful install and upgrade cycle of late-2000s mobile apps. The company is inactive (YC lists it as Inactive; reporting describes the startup as shut down after raising roughly $2M), the tsumobi.com domain no longer serves a website, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or specifications were found. This profile is retained as a historical a16z portfolio record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: VonBox
providers.description: VonBox operated as Vonjour (vonjour.com), a Santa Monica, CA cloud communications startup offering phone, text messaging, and contact center services for small businesses, backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups) and Kima Ventures circa 2014-2015, including a Vonjour for 500 Startups perk program. The vonjour.com website is no longer live (DNS resolves but HTTP does not respond), and no public API, developer documentation, or client packages are published. The founding team (Daniel Tawfik, Aman Fahimullah) went on to build ZenPatient (zenpatient.com), a digital health platform, and the company GitHub organization github.com/Vonjour is now branded ZenPatient.

providers.name: Attotude
providers.description: AttoTude is a semiconductor and data-center infrastructure company building the first wired terahertz (THz) interconnect for AI and hyperscale networking. Its platform pairs the AttoEngine, an ASIC-based THz radio built on standard CMOS manufacturing, with AttoWire, a low-loss dielectric waveguide that carries 200/400/800 Gbit/s per lane over reaches up to roughly 40 meters, delivering the bandwidth density of optics without the cost, power, and complexity of photonics. Founded to relieve the interconnect bottleneck in everything-to-everything AI clusters, the company has raised roughly $143M across seed, Series A, Series B, and Series C rounds. This is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or SDK; the profile below is enriched only with the identity and domain-security facts the pipeline could verify.

providers.name: HUB Group
providers.description: HUB is a global leader in multifunction pole design and street infrastructure, supplying over 1,000 pieces of urban infrastructure worldwide. With 20+ years of experience, HUB excels in integrating digital devices and data analytics into innovative urban solutions. Partnered with Valmont Industries, HUB delivers high-quality infrastructure for public spaces, including telecommunications poles, monopoles, steel jackets, and head frames.

providers.name: Avaya
providers.description: Avaya delivers smarter customer experiences, greater business efficiency, and lower costs through AI-powered communication and collaboration tools.

providers.name: Ericsson
providers.description: Ericsson (Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson) is a Swedish multinational networking and telecommunications equipment vendor headquartered in Kista, Stockholm. Founded in 1876, the company supplies mobile and fixed network infrastructure to communication service providers worldwide and operates across three product areas: Networks (5G RAN, 5G Core, Cloud RAN, transport), Cloud Software & Services (OSS/BSS, orchestration, billing, charging, analytics), and Enterprise Wireless Solutions (private 5G via Cradlepoint). Ericsson holds more than 60,000 granted patents and operates 21 R&D centers, with networks that carry roughly 40 percent of the world's mobile data traffic. In 2024 Ericsson and twelve major operators — AT&T, Bharti Airtel, Deutsche Telekom, KDDI, Orange, Reliance Jio, Singtel, Telefonica, Telstra, T-Mobile, Verizon, and Vodafone — closed Aduna, a 50:50 joint venture that aggregates CAMARA-aligned network APIs (SIM Swap, Number Verification, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Device Reachability, Scam Signal, Call Forwarding Signal, Connectivity Insights, OTP SMS) and exposes them through hyperscaler and CPaaS channel partners (Microsoft Azure Marketplace, Google Cloud, Vonage, Sinch, Infobip). Ericsson also owns Vonage (acquired 2022), which operates the public-facing developer portal for many of these network capabilities, and runs the Ericsson Intelligent Automation Platform (EIAP) for ORAN-aligned rApp development. Ericsson does not publish a single consolidated developer portal or canonical OpenAPI catalog at ericsson.com — its programmable surface is delivered indirectly through Aduna, Vonage, and channel partners, and most of its public GitHub presence is research tooling and infrastructure software (CodeChecker, CodeCompass, ecchronos) rather than developer-facing APIs.

providers.name: Talk Labs
providers.description: Talk Labs (TalkLabs) builds AI-powered voice simulations for corporate learning, turning training theory into practical, hands-on skills. Its platform provides AI trainers that role-play realistic customer scenarios so frontline sales and customer-service staff can practice conversations on demand. Capabilities include 24/7 AI coaching with no capacity limits, voice-based simulations in 50+ languages, progress-tracking and analytics dashboards, LMS integration, and a no-code AI lesson builder, with deployment within a week of contract. It serves banks, retail, hospitality, financial services, and restaurants. Backed by 500 Global and founded by Serge Sarkisian (CEO) and Ilia Krotov (CTO). No public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Tellabs
providers.description: Tellabs is a networking infrastructure vendor focused on Passive Optical LAN (OLAN) and broadband access for enterprises, government, and service providers. Its portfolio includes the Passive Optical LAN solution, the Tellabs 1000 MSAP broadband digital loop carrier converging legacy copper and fiber, and the Tellabs Panorama Element/Integrated Network Manager (EMS/INM) for SDN-style management of optical LANs. Tellabs also runs a Technical Assistance Center, professional services, training, and a partner program. As of this enrichment pass, Tellabs publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification; its Panorama products reference a North Bound Interface (NBI) for back-office automation, but no OpenAPI/Swagger or public API documentation is available.

providers.name: Broadsoft
providers.description: BroadSoft was a cloud unified-communications (UCaaS) and VoIP software provider whose BroadWorks and BroadCloud platforms powered hosted PBX, calling, messaging, and contact-center services for telecom carriers and service providers worldwide. Its developer surface centered on the Xtended Services Interface (XSI) and OCI (Open Client Interface) provisioning APIs. Cisco acquired BroadSoft in February 2018 and folded the products into its Collaboration portfolio; the platform now ships as Cisco BroadWorks. The independent developer presence has been retired — www.broadsoft.com 301-redirects to cisco.com — so this profile carries no standalone live API surface. Originally surfaced as a bessemer-venture-partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Eltek
providers.description: Eltek is a Norwegian power-electronics and telecom power-systems manufacturer (DC power rectifiers, industrial and telecom energy systems, the Flatpack product family) now operating as part of Delta Electronics. Its primary domain eltek.com 301-redirects to Delta's standard telecom power solutions catalog (www.delta-emea.com). This is a physical-hardware brand: no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface was found. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub via the sierra-ventures VC pipeline; profile retained for domain-security signal and future re-check.

providers.name: Integration Patterns
providers.description: Integration Patterns are design patterns and best practices for integrating different software systems and applications, including messaging, data transformation, and service orchestration approaches. Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), as cataloged by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, provide a technology-independent vocabulary and visual notation harvested from proven solutions to recurring integration problems, organized into Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

providers.name: Marvell Technology
providers.description: Marvell Technology, Inc. is a Fortune 500 fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company designs and develops data infrastructure semiconductor solutions including custom ASICs, data processing units, Ethernet controllers, optical and copper PHYs, switches, and storage controllers used in data centers, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, automotive, and consumer markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Marvell. Public developer documentation is gated behind a customer support portal and is not openly accessible.

providers.name: Masmovil
providers.description: Masmovil (MasMovil Group) is a Spanish telecommunications operator providing mobile, fiber optic internet, and fixed-line services to consumers and businesses across Spain, with bundled fiber-plus-mobile packages, device sales, roaming, and international calling. The group operates a family of consumer telecom brands and, following its 2024 combination with Orange Spain, is part of the MasOrange joint venture. As of this enrichment pass Masmovil publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; the network profile carries the identity and a domain security posture probe only.

providers.name: MetroPCS
providers.description: MetroPCS is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Altitude Software
providers.description: Altitude Software is a contact center and unified customer interaction (uCI) software company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal. Its flagship Altitude uCI suite provides omnichannel contact center capabilities — inbound/outbound campaigns, IVR and self-service, routing, dialer, recording and quality management, and CRM/ERP integration — with the Altitude uAgent SDK exposing Java, C/C++, .NET, SOAP, XML-RPC and web-service APIs for on-premises and cloud deployments. Altitude Software was a portfolio company of Insight Partners and was acquired by Enghouse Systems (TSX: ENGH) on 2020-12-30; the product line is now developed and maintained by Enghouse Interactive, and the brand continues to operate regionally (e.g. Altitude Software APAC). The company does not publish a modern public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; integration is delivered through the proprietary uAgent SDK and packaged CRM/ERP connectors.

providers.name: Blue Jeans Network
providers.description: Blue Jeans Network (later BlueJeans by Verizon) was a cloud-based video conferencing company founded in 2009 in Mountain View / San Jose, California. It delivered interoperable video meetings across desktop, mobile, and conference-room systems, and offered a developer surface that included the onVideo/Meetings REST API and a WebRTC Embed SDK for embedding live video into applications. Verizon acquired BlueJeans in 2020; Verizon subsequently discontinued the BlueJeans service and the bluejeans.com website and developer portal are no longer reachable. This profile preserves the company's published package artifacts, which persist in public registries even though the hosted service is retired. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Battery Ventures.

providers.name: National Telecommunications and Information Administration
providers.description: The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) is an agency of the U.S. Department of Commerce that serves as the executive branch principal advisor on telecommunications and information policy issues.

providers.name: Network Protocols
providers.description: Network protocols are the standardized rules and conventions for communication between network devices. They include foundational protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, BGP, SMTP, FTP, SSH and many others that enable data exchange across networks. Network protocols are fundamental to modern network architectures and underpin reliable communication between systems.

providers.name: Daero Group
providers.description: DAERO (Daero Group) is a construction-technology company building mobile-first tools for trades and field teams. Its flagship product, ZeroPunch, is a field-operations platform that turns real-time field intuition into structured construction data: voice-first capture lets crews speak field observations in natural language, photos are paired with contextual field data, work is auto-assigned by scope, and stream-of-consciousness notes are converted into organized daily logs. ZeroPunch offers a two-way integration with Procore for project-management sync. The company positions itself around the daily needs of the people actually doing the work, aiming to make construction operations smarter and faster. As of this profile DAERO publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is partnership-level (Procore) and inquiries go to support@daerogroup.com. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Daze
providers.description: Daze is a mobile "freeform chat" application for iOS and Android, published by Marble Media (Android package com.marblemedia.dazechat, iOS App Store id 6497405419). It is a consumer social messaging product with an active Discord community and is venture-backed by a16z, Kindred Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, Daze exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface (all /.well-known/ and /llms.txt probes returned 404); it is a consumer app rather than an API provider. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company record.

providers.name: Empirix
providers.description: Empirix was a communications and contact-center test, assurance, and monitoring company backed by Matrix Partners. Its products spanned network and application performance testing, VoIP and IVR quality assurance, contact-center monitoring, and end-to-end customer-experience assurance for carriers and enterprises. Empirix was acquired by Infovista in 2020; its testing and monitoring portfolio now operates under the Hammer Technologies brand, which is evolving into VistaCX (Voice Explorer, CallMaster, VoiceWatch, HammerRTC, VistaOne). The company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; empirix.com now redirects to hammer.com. This profile is a network stub enriched from public web surfaces only.

providers.name: Mybots.pro
providers.description: myBots (operated by Global AI Group, Inc.) builds enterprise AI sales and support agents for messaging channels — WhatsApp, Instagram, Telegram, and web chat. Each agent qualifies inbound leads, answers questions in the business's brand voice, books appointments on a connected calendar (Calendly), and runs 24/7 across every messenger a company operates. It is a no-developer SaaS aimed at business teams; as of this profile the product exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or documented webhook surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nextgentel
providers.description: NextGenTel is one of Norway's established independent internet service providers, delivering fiber and DSL broadband, TV (via RiksTV), mobile telephony, and online security services to consumers and small businesses across Norway. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass (2026-07-20) found a consumer-facing marketing and self-service website (www.nextgentel.no) and a customer help center (hjelp.nextgentel.no), but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or programmatic API surface — this remains a consumer telecom company with no external API program.

providers.name: The Nudge
providers.description: The Nudge is a free consumer lifestyle app that texts its members short videos from locals recommending their favorite real-world things to do — secret hikes, date ideas, restaurants, and activities — a few "Nudges" each week to help people (primarily millennials) have more fun in real life and be more adventurous, romantic, and social. Founded in 2018 by siblings Sarah and John Peterson and based in San Francisco, The Nudge is available on iOS and Android and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners among other investors. It is a business-to-consumer product delivered over SMS and mobile apps, with no public API or developer program.

providers.name: eBPF Foundation
providers.description: The eBPF Foundation is a Linux Foundation project that advances eBPF technology by guiding upstream development, promoting its benefits, and enhancing its security and reliability. eBPF enables programmable kernel functionality for networking, observability, tracing, and security without changing kernel source code. The Foundation itself does not operate a public API; it stewards the technology and community.

providers.name: LotusFlare
providers.description: LotusFlare is a cloud-native digital commerce and monetization platform for telecommunications operators. Its Digital Network Operator (DNO) Cloud provides charging, product catalog, ordering, and digital customer-experience (BSS) capabilities as a managed SaaS to mobile carriers, and powers eSIM and travel-connectivity brands. The platform is delivered to enterprise telecom customers rather than through a public self-serve developer API; no public developer portal or API definition was discoverable at profile time. Backed by GV and Social Capital.

providers.name: Snips
providers.description: Snips was a Paris-based artificial intelligence company that built a private-by-design, on-device voice assistant platform and natural language understanding (NLU) technology, letting developers add offline voice interfaces to connected devices without sending audio to the cloud. Snips was acquired by Sonos in November 2019 and its team became the Sonos Voice Experience group; the developer platform, hosted APIs, and console were subsequently discontinued. snips.ai now serves only a static acquisition-announcement page, and the company's open-source libraries (notably the Snips NLU engine) remain archived under the github.com/snipsco organization.

providers.name: Stickies
providers.description: Stickies (stickies.wtf) was a Los Angeles-based consumer web3 company, built by BYO Labs, that made "dumb stickers and GIFs starring your favorite NFTs" — users connected a crypto wallet holding their NFTs and generated custom stickers and GIFs of those avatars for use in messaging and social apps. Founded around 2022 by Tom Wright (CEO) and Sterling Barnett (COO), it raised roughly $5.5M with backing from Lightspeed Venture Partners (Jeremy Liew). The product was a closed consumer web app with no public developer API, documentation, or SDK. The company appears defunct: the stickies.wtf site was last captured live in 2023, returned 403s by mid-2024, and the domain no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) as of July 2026; co-founder Sterling Barnett has since moved on to other ventures.

providers.name: Tribes
providers.description: Tribes (Tribes Protocol, Inc.) is a web3-native social wallet and messaging application that lets people co-own and manage digital assets together while communicating directly from within the wallet itself. Its "co-wallets" combine group messaging and shared custody so crypto communities, creators, and DAOs can coordinate and make decisions without relying on external tools like Discord or Twitter. Founded by former Coinbase engineer Hish Bouabdallah, Tribes raised a $3.3M pre-seed round in January 2023 led by Kindred Ventures, with South Park Commons and Script Capital. It is a consumer crypto product; its public code surface is the tribes-protocol GitHub organization (smart-contract libraries and tooling) rather than a hosted REST/GraphQL developer API.

providers.name: Trustid
providers.description: TRUSTID was a Portland, Oregon telephone caller-authentication and call-center anti-fraud company led by CEO Patrick Cox, authenticating inbound callers pre-answer without knowledge-based interrogation of the caller. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures, TRUSTID was acquired by Neustar (closed January 2019), and Neustar was itself acquired by TransUnion in December 2021, where the caller-authentication capability lives on in Trusted Call Solutions. TRUSTID no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface — trustid.com is unresponsive and www.trustid.com returns HTTP 503 from Neustar redirect infrastructure.

providers.name: Ubiquisys
providers.description: Ubiquisys was a UK-based developer of intelligent 3G/LTE/Wi-Fi small cells and femtocells for mobile operators, with products like ActiveRadio, ActiveSON, CloudBase, and EdgeCloud deployed by carriers such as SFR and SoftBank, and was ranked #1 in ABI Research's Small Cell Vendor Matrix. Backed by Accel, Cisco announced its intent to acquire Ubiquisys on April 3, 2013, and the company was absorbed into Cisco's small cell portfolio; ubiquisys.com is now Cisco-owned and redirects to Cisco's acquisitions page. Ubiquisys published no public API or developer surface.
